entries.abstract: Every homeomorphism between arbitrary subsets of completely metrizable spaces extends to a homeomorphism between Gδ supersets contained in the respective closures. Empty subsets and ambient spaces are included. A zero-oscillation construction first gives a Gδ continuous extension domain for maps to complete metric spaces. Restricting the two continuous extensions gives mutually inverse maps. The arbitrary supplied topologies are preserved by compatible complete metrics. Classical mathematics, with no mathematical novelty or priority claim.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Lavrentieff's Gδ homeomorphism extension theorem

entries.abstract: Lean formalization of spanning-tree maximization over finite connected induced subgraphs of the square lattice. The development establishes edge isoperimetry of every maximizer, the maximum count and all maximizing lattice-isometry classes at every positive cardinality, and uniqueness of the canonical corner-strip domain for N >= 18. Nonuniqueness occurs exactly at N = 3, 8, 10, 13; the canonical count has exceptions at N = 7, 14, 17. It also establishes the sharp square-cardinality stability inequality, an exact scalar product formula and rational recurrence for corner-strip counts, the global extremal asymptotic expansion with O(N^(-1/2)) remainder, and the appendix's exact strip-energy Fourier identity, rectangular remainders, Green estimates, and explicit bounds.
entries.title: Spanning-Tree Maximization Forces Isoperimetry in the Square Lattice

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Mader's 1972 theorem in the form of Diestel's Theorem 1.4.3: for k ≥ 1, every nonempty finite simple graph with average degree at least 4k has a (k + 1)-connected induced subgraph H with e(H)/|H| > e(G)/|G| − k. Vertex connectivity is defined by deletion of fewer than k vertices (same definition as in the Menger–Hamiltonicity entry). Mathlib does not contain vertex connectivity or this theorem.
entries.title: Mader's theorem on highly connected subgraphs

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of a fixed-parameter theorem of "Maximum-weight independent set in embedded graphs parameterized by Euler genus and number of odd faces" (forthcoming), with a provably correct implementation of the algorithm as one fixed program for an explicit sixteen-register pointer machine. Lean proves that for every graph drawn in a closed surface of Euler genus gamma whose complement has k regions of odd total boundary length, and all integer vertex weights, the program outputs a maximum-weight independent set within 2^(c (p size(p) + 1)) (N size(M))^c bit operations, where p = gamma + k, N = |V| + |E| + 1, M = max(1, max |w_v|), size(x) is the binary length of x and c is an absolute constant; that is, 2^O(p log(p+1)) poly(N, log(M+1)) with an absolute polynomial exponent. Surfaces are represented by finite combinatorial flag maps; orientable and nonorientable surfaces, disconnected and noncellular drawings, loops, multiple edges, isolated vertices and negative weights are covered. The algorithm solves one exact linear program per retained component over a finite-group network whose size depends only on p, using exact integral quotient coordinates, midpoint convexity of class minima and a coarse Jensen inequality, and recovers an optimal set from perturbed edge costs. The cost is a logarithmic bit-cost measure including an explicit stack simulation of recursive calls. The proofs use exactly propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: An FPT Algorithm for Maximum-Weight Independent Set in Embedded Graphs, in Lean 4

entries.abstract: For k ≥ 2 let n_k be the least n ≥ 2k such that n − i divides the binomial coefficient C(n, k) for all but exactly one 0 ≤ i < k (Erdős Problem 1063; Erdős and Selfridge 1983; OEIS A389360; Guy's Unsolved Problems in Number Theory, B31). Using the definition of n_k from google-deepmind/formal-conjectures verbatim, this project proves two results in Lean 4 with Mathlib. (1) For every k ≥ 2, n_k ≥ W'_k = ∏_{p^a ∥ k} p^(a + ⌊log_p(k − 1)⌋); the bound is attained in the sense that n_k − i₀ = W'_k for k = 4, 6, 14. (2) If n ≥ 2k, e < k, and every n − i with 0 ≤ i < k, i ≠ e, divides C(n, k), then e = n mod k and D(k, e) = ∏_{p^a ∥ k} p^(a + v_p(C(k − 1, e)) + ⌊log_p max(e, k − 1 − e)⌋) divides n − e. Result (2) was proved informally by the user rickyc in the erdosproblems.com discussion thread for the problem. It is the structural input of the exhaustive searches that extend the OEIS table (by jbell31 for 60 ≤ k ≤ 75, and by the author for k up to 140): an admissible n with exceptional index e must lie in the residue class e modulo D(k, e). This formalization makes the minimality of those computed values depend only on verified mathematics and on the search code; jbell31 had noted in the thread that a Lean proof of this divisibility would close that gap. formal-conjectures records upper bounds and small values of n_k but no general lower bound. The development also proves the Erdős–Selfridge observation and that Cambie's number k · lcm(1, …, k − 1) is admissible, so the lower bound holds for every k ≥ 2 without further assumptions.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 1063: a lower bound for n_k and the structure of the exceptional index

entries.abstract: Typed triangle decomposition results from Paper II: a typical-host theorem under three-step links for four-label families; its nearly complete and balanced deductions with explicit type-weight hypotheses; a semidense two-label mixed-triangle theorem; a computer-assisted typical-host theorem for every admissible four-label family; and a terminal absorber obtained from a bounded signed certificate and explicit physical hinge supply. Divisibility includes global edge counts and local degree profiles. The typical-host hypotheses are retained; the result is not asserted for arbitrary divisible hosts. The repository contains the substantive proof development, including the finite family census and conserved-family constructions, with a small independent Mathlib-only Challenge.
entries.title: Robust absorption for typed triangles

entries.abstract: For every coprime pair a > b ≥ 1 there is a straight-line derivation of gcd(a, b) that uses only the remainder operation on available values and makes at most (6 + o(1)) log₂ a / log₂ log₂ a remainder calls, uniformly in b ≤ a; Euclid's algorithm needs about 1.44 log₂ a calls in the worst case. The proof stores a prefix of the Euclidean remainder sequence, shows that its consecutive pairs stay distinct modulo every sufficiently large modulus, and uses close residues to shrink the modulus by three remainder calls at a time. Consequently the intrinsic calls(rem)-complexities of the gcd and of coprimeness, in the sense of Moschovakis's Abstract Recursion and Intrinsic Complexity, are O(log a / log log a). This refutes Conjecture 3.4 of Moschovakis's 2012 notes "Absolute lower bounds for uniform processes" and the version (4F-5) of the Main Conjecture in the book, both for the structure (ℕ, rem, eq0) and for Nε = (ℕ, rem, eq0, eq1). The Main Conjecture for algorithms (deterministic or nondeterministic recursive programs) is not addressed and remains open. Lower bounds are also formalized: every gcd certificate needs at least as many remainder facts as the shortest derivation, and the coprimeness complexity is at least (1 − ε) log₂ log₂ N on all but o(N²) coprime pairs below N.
entries.title: The Euclidean algorithm is not optimal among uniform processes

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the theorem that almost all graphs are determined by their generalized spectrum, which is Haemers' conjecture for the generalized spectrum. The generalized spectrum of a graph is the spectrum of its adjacency matrix A together with the spectrum of the adjacency matrix J - I - A of its complement, and a graph is determined by its generalized spectrum (DGS) if every graph with the same generalized spectrum is isomorphic to it. The main theorem, DGSMain.almost_all_graphs_are_DGS, states that the proportion of the graphs on the vertex set {0, ..., n-1} that are DGS tends to 1 as n tends to infinity; that is, the random graph G(n, 1/2) is DGS with probability tending to one. This is Theorem 1.1 of the accompanying paper, and the formalization contains its whole proof: the reduction to local failures at primes through the rational orthogonal matrices relating generalized cospectral graphs, Seidel switching, Fourier analysis of random symmetric matrices over finite rings, inverse Littlewood-Offord estimates over finite fields, rank estimates for random symmetric matrices modulo primes, and the exclusion of rational factors of the characteristic polynomial of a random symmetric sign matrix with zero diagonal. The results that the paper quotes from the literature are also proved: Kneser's addition theorem, the theorem of Johnson and Newman on generalized cospectral graphs, and the cases used of the theorems of Tao and Vu (a random symmetric sign matrix has simple spectrum) and of O'Rourke and Touri (G(n, 1/2) is controllable), the last two by a new argument based on the methods of the paper. The proof uses only the standard axioms propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice.
entries.title: Almost all graphs are determined by their generalized spectrum

entries.abstract: For the two-dimensional nearest-neighbor RP2 and RP3 director models, the absolute quadrupolar two-point correlation is bounded by C exp(-c (log(2+r))^2) at every finite bound on the dimensionless coupling. The positive constants are uniform over finite square-lattice subgraphs, arbitrary signed edge couplings within that bound, and observation sites; r is the integer lattice infinity distance. The compared statements use explicit normalized spherical product measures and Gibbs-integral quotients, with observable (n_x dot n_y)^2 - 1/3 or - 1/4, respectively. No response estimate or decay certificate is assumed. This registry interface selects the two finite-volume bounds. It does not assert exponential decay at all temperatures or the absence of every thermodynamic or topological transition. The larger development also contains local-limit and high-temperature results, which are not selected by this Comparator entry.
entries.title: Log-square quadrupolar correlation decay in two-dimensional RP2 and RP3 models

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization project for (F) an explicit two-parameter family of minimally five-generated numerical semigroups <m, m+1, m+k, m+2k-1, m+2k>, m = 2kq+1, whose toric ideal has spanRank exactly 4k+2. Planned scope for (W), a proposed finite-width bound beta1 <= 2w+2 (4 <= w <= 40), not all formalized: the generic fiber-graph infrastructure, both algebraic bridges (only the upper bridge is formalized; the reverse bridge is not), the corrected singleton-counting decomposition beta1 + p = 5 + N, the pair-component antichain lemma and certificate-checker soundness (not yet written). Version 1 targets F; W is stated and excluded from the release comparator. F is sorry-free at 793e759.
entries.title: First Betti numbers of five-generated numerical semigroups

entries.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem that every temporal clique on n vertices admits a temporal spanner with O(n log n) edges. A temporal clique is the complete graph on a finite vertex set whose edges carry natural-number time labels, locally injective (two edges sharing an endpoint have distinct labels); a temporal spanner is a set of edges in which every vertex reaches every other one by a journey with non-decreasing labels. The result is due to Casteigts, Peters and Schoeters (ICALP 2019, JCSS 2021); the formal proof follows the dismountability-only proof of Carnevale, Casteigts and Corsini (SAND 2025, §§2–4), which reduces cliques to bi-cliques and concludes with the one-sided dismountability of Angrick et al. (ESA 2024). The compared statements give an explicit bound of 2n⌈log₂ n⌉ + 4n edges and the asymptotic O(n log n) form with a bound function chosen uniformly for all cliques. The work is supervised by Arnaud Casteigts and Karine Altisen.
entries.title: Temporal cliques admit spanners of size O(n log n)

entries.abstract: Lean 4 development (no Mathlib) of the mathematics, algorithms and security statements of Morse, Alqaradaghi and Kozsik, "Control flow obfuscation with irreducible loops and self-modifying code": a self-modifying-code solver for 2-SAT and the planted instance generator as an algorithm, the extremal numbers of irreducible loops and multiple-entry edges (the families Kn and Mn), the irreducible-loop transformations of Figures 5 and 6, the Boolean control-flow graphs of AES, and the security statements of Section 5.1 relative to an explicit structural threat model. Two Challenges are submitted from one development: Challenge.lean (solver, extremal numbers, transformations, security model) and ChallengeAES.lean (the AES graphs); a Challenge may have at most 1,000 lines.
entries.title: Control flow obfuscation with irreducible loops and self-modifying code

entries.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization accompanying S. Vorobev, "On the inclusion D_5(G) ⊆ γ_4(G): reductions, the Lie-ring proof, and evidence" (preprint, 2026; submitted to arXiv math.GR on 2026-10-22). The integral dimension subgroups D_n(G) = {g ∈ G : g − 1 ∈ Δ(G)^n} are defined from the augmentation ideal of Mathlib's integral group ring. Kourovka Problem 20.84 asks whether D_5(G) ⊆ γ_4(G) for every group; it is open and is not claimed here. Unconditional results: D_5(G) = γ_5(G) whenever G/γ_2(G) is finite of exponent 3, and more generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group whose cubes form a cyclic group (paper, Theorems 6.6 and 6.8; the inclusion part of Tahara's 1981 description of D_5 is formalized for this); D_5(G) lies in the Jennings product M_5(G) for finite 2-groups of class at most 3; and, for "candidates" (the paper's minimal-counterexample shape among finite 2-groups of class 3), there is no candidate of order 2^11 with Q/P_3 ≅ Z/4 × (Z/2)^7 and none of order 2^11 and rank at least 8 (paper, Lemma 5.6 and Proposition 5.7). Conditional results, with every assumption an explicit hypothesis: the reduction of Problem 20.84 to finite 2-groups of class exactly 3 assuming D_3 = γ_3, Passi's D_4^2 ⊆ γ_4 and Gruenberg's residual theorem (Proposition 2.1); a minimal counterexample is a candidate assuming D_3 = γ_3 (Lemma 5.2); and D_5 = 1 for groups of order 2^11, class at most 3 and rank at least 8, assuming D_3 = γ_3 and the paper's computer result for order 2^10 (Proposition 5.7, D_5 form).
entries.title: Fifth dimension subgroups: D₅ = γ₅ when G/γ₂ is finite of exponent 3, candidates for a counterexample, and a reduction of Kourovka 20.84

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Graham–Pollak theorem: the edge set of the complete graph K_n cannot be partitioned into fewer than n − 1 complete bipartite graphs, together with the matching construction by n − 1 stars. Biclique decompositions are encoded by families of pairs of disjoint vertex sets covering every pair of distinct vertices exactly once. Mathlib does not contain this theorem.
entries.title: The Graham–Pollak theorem

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of effective dynamics near spectrally stable planar fronts in reaction-diffusion systems under small, bounded uniformly continuous perturbations. The main result constructs global solutions and approximates the perturbed front by a phase evolving according to a viscous Hamilton-Jacobi equation, with a uniform quantitative error bound.
entries.title: Stability of planar fronts in reaction-diffusion systems

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 formalization, built on Mathlib, of two classical theorems of Bautista, Gabriel, Roiter and Salmerón on finite-dimensional representation-finite algebras over an algebraically closed field. Theorem A: every such algebra, in any characteristic, has a normed multiplicative basis, that is, a basis containing a complete set of primitive orthogonal idempotents, closed under products up to zero, and meeting every power of the Jacobson radical in a basis of that power. Theorem B: every basic such algebra over a field of characteristic different from two is standard, that is, its category of indecomposable modules is equivalent to the mesh category of its Auslander–Reiten quiver by an equivalence sending each vertex to its module. The proof follows the deformation-theoretic approach of the formalized manuscript: the standard form is the graded algebra of the radical filtration of the category of indecomposable modules, and the original algebra is recovered as a filtered deformation of it. The Auslander–Reiten theory used is proved in the library.
entries.title: Multiplicative bases and standardness of representation-finite algebras

entries.abstract: Every nonempty countable metrizable topological space without isolated points is homeomorphic to the rational numbers with their usual topology. Conversely, these four properties characterize spaces homeomorphic to the rationals. A clopen basis is derived from the hypotheses. Scheduled binary clopen splits give each point an address with both bits arbitrarily far out; the induced lexicographic order is proved dense, without endpoints, and to generate exactly the original topology. The countable dense-order isomorphism theorem then gives the homeomorphism. This formalizes classical mathematics; no mathematical novelty or priority claim is made.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Sierpiński's characterization of the rationals

entries.abstract: For every configuration on the integer plane over an arbitrary finite alphabet, a positive k by n rectangle with at most k*n occurring translated patterns forces a nonzero global period of the original configuration. The statement includes equality at the complexity threshold and rectangles of width or height one. The proof formalizes Pranava Kumar's manuscript through Laurent annihilators, a sharp periodic-wedge complexity bound, generating polygons, and selection of the same nonperiodic orbit point throughout the periodic-background construction. Its mathematical setting is multidimensional symbolic dynamics and combinatorics of low-complexity configurations. The independent Challenge states the full conjecture using only standard Mathlib notions.
entries.title: Nivat's conjecture: formalization of Pranava Kumar's argument

entries.abstract: A topological space is homeomorphic to Cantor space, the countable product of discrete Boolean spaces, if and only if it is nonempty, compact, metrizable, has a basis of clopen sets, and has no isolated points. A full binary clopen scheme decides an enumerated basis one element at each depth. Its point-address map is continuous; compact nested intersections realize every binary branch, and basis decisions separate points. A continuous bijection from a compact space to the Hausdorff Cantor space is a homeomorphism. This formalizes a classical theorem of Brouwer; no mathematical novelty or priority claim is made.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Brouwer characterization of Cantor space

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Bondy–Simonovits theorem: for every k ≥ 2 there is a constant C such that every finite simple graph on n vertices with no cycle of length exactly 2k has at most C·n^(1+1/k) edges, i.e. ex(n, C_2k) = O(n^(1+1/k)). The statement is existential in C (the proof gives C = 16k + 4); the sharper constants of later work and the full range of even cycle lengths in Bondy–Simonovits's paper are not stated. Mathlib has walks and cycles but not this theorem.
entries.title: The Bondy–Simonovits even cycle theorem

entries.abstract: A topological space is homeomorphic to Baire space, the countable product of discrete natural numbers, if and only if it is nonempty, Polish, has a basis of clopen sets, and every compact subset has empty interior. The construction partitions each nonempty clopen set into countably infinitely many distinct nonempty clopen children with arbitrarily small diameter. A fully branching shrinking scheme gives a continuous open bijective limit map and therefore a homeomorphism. The converse uses finite coordinate images of compact Baire subsets. This formalizes a classical theorem of Alexandrov and Urysohn; no novelty or priority claim is made.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Alexandrov–Urysohn characterization of Baire space

entries.abstract: Every nonempty Polish space is the image of Baire space, the product of countably many discrete natural-number spaces, under a continuous open surjection. The proof constructs a countably branching nonempty open scheme with nested closures, covering children and geometrically shrinking diameters. The image of each basic cylinder is proved exactly equal to its scheme open set. This yields openness and surjectivity of the limit map; existence is also characterized by nonemptiness. These are classical results, with no novelty or priority claim.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Open Baire-space representation of Polish spaces

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of R. M. Wilson's "Nonisomorphic Steiner triple systems" (inequality (2.1), Theorems 1–4, Lemmas 3–5, including the exact numbers of Latin squares of orders 6, 7 and 8 and the bounds N(19) ≥ 2450, N(21) ≥ 2160980, N(25) ≥ 163929929318400) and of N. Linial and Z. Luria's "An upper bound on the number of Steiner triple systems" (Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 with explicit error terms). Version 2 adds a proof of the van der Waerden permanent theorem (Egorychev, Falikman), following Gurvits's proof as simplified by Laurent and Schrijver. The parts of Wilson's Theorems 2 and 3 that rely on it are stated both as implications from the hypothesis vdWPC, as in the paper, and unconditionally (theorem2_full, theorem3_full). Finite computations are kernel-checked certificates (no native_decide). Mathlib does not contain these results.
entries.title: Counting Steiner triple systems: Wilson (1974) and Linial–Luria (2013)

entries.abstract: For the reciprocal series with denominators n! - 1, the selected Lean theorems give an exact carry characterization of rationality, divisor-channel coordinates, and a finite gcd moment certificate. Companion-orbit and complementary tail criteria are included with their stated hypotheses. These structural results do not certify the paper's large computed denominator exclusions or resolve the irrationality question.
entries.title: Carry and divisor-channel criteria for the factorial-minus-one reciprocal series

entries.abstract: For coprime integers a > b >= 1 satisfying b^μ < a, equivalently log b / log a < θ*, the selected Lean theorems prove irrationality of F(a/b). They include the base 31/4 and every positive integer power, plus associated irrationality-measure bounds. The region excludes 3/2. This configuration does not select the paper's later sharp fixed-base asymptotic or all-rank Hankel results.
entries.title: An explicit rational-base irrationality region for Zudilin's Lambert series

entries.abstract: For pairwise distinct primes p, q and r, the three-prime reciprocal running-LCM kernel has nonzero square minors of every order, with row and column indices chosen independently of the third exponent. Consequently it admits no finite rational separated representation. The selected entry also proves an exact rank formula for threshold-column matrices, an explicit two-by-two example at 2,3,5, separation in the two-prime comparison, and the four-base dyadic recurrence for the actual 2,3,5 sum. A uniform finite-rank approximation statement concerns the rescaled carry matrix. The stronger unit-determinant modular minors are in E269_08 and are outside this configuration. Infinite kernel rank does not prove irrationality of the running-LCM series. In the selected rank theorem the determinants remain nonzero for every fixed third exponent k using the same injective row and column maps. The distance theorem concerns a rescaled real carry matrix and is not an approximation lower bound for the original summable kernel.
entries.title: Infinite rank of the three-prime running-LCM kernel

entries.abstract: Given any convergent dyadic series with nonnegative integer coefficients, any finite prefix and any eventually unbounded correction allowance, one common permitted set of upper Banach density zero supports nonnegative integer corrections realising every target in a nondegenerate interval above the original sum. Each fixed modulus eventually divides both corrections and cumulative corrections beyond a cutoff independent of the target. With polylogarithmic allowance, the selected theorem also bounds support in dyadic windows and preserves empirical block distributions in total variation for lengths o(log log X), uniformly in the target. The entry additionally states exact prime-to-gap summation identities and tail rationality criteria. It does not select the prime-gap joint countermodel, which in the paper uses named outside inputs, and makes no claim that corrected cumulative positions are prime or that the original prime series is irrational.
entries.title: Uniform sparse rationalisation of dyadic series

entries.abstract: Every positive strictly increasing zero-indexed integer sequence a with n^3(a_n^2/a_(n+1) - 1 - 3/n) tending to zero has an irrational reciprocal sum. The entry also states the exact integer-tail and number-field steps used to exclude the resulting cubic profile: positive-density exceptions, primitive gcd reduction, square specialisation, scale twelve, forbidden words modulo seven, and regular-rate extraction. The printed one-indexed paper theorem uses its stated finite-prefix argument. The separate bounded-increment Sylvester criterion in the paper is outside this configuration, and the unrestricted Erdős problem #243 remains open. The selected Challenge explicitly retains the strict monotonicity and positivity of a, the HasSum witness for its reciprocal series, and the n³-scaled rate limit. It does not silently infer that rate from the weaker condition a_(n+1)/a_n² → 1.
entries.title: Cubic-rate irrationality for reciprocal sums

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two basic results of spectral graph theory, stated through the adjacency quadratic form on vectors orthogonal to the all-ones vector: the expander mixing lemma of Alon and Chung (for a d-regular graph on n ≥ 2 vertices with |x·Ax| ≤ μ‖x‖² on 𝟙⊥, |e(S,T) − d|S||T|/n| ≤ μ√(|S||T|)), and the Alon–Boppana bound in Nilli's form (a d-regular graph, d ≥ 2, with two vertices at distance at least 2k + 4 has a nonzero x ⟂ 𝟙 with x·Ax ≥ (2√(d−1) − (2√(d−1) − 1)/(k+1))‖x‖²). Mathlib has adjacency matrices but neither result.
entries.title: The expander mixing lemma and the Alon–Boppana bound

entries.abstract: Continuous open surjections preserve the strong Choquet property in arbitrary topological spaces. An explicit full-history strategy lifts each legal target play coherently, keeps the marked point, and maps an actual common source point. Consequently a continuous open metrizable image of a Polish space is Polish. A second-countable completely metrizable source gives a completely metrizable metrizable image. A regular Hausdorff codomain also suffices, by inherited second countability and Urysohn metrizability. These are classical results; no novelty or priority is claimed.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Continuous open images of Polish spaces

entries.abstract: Formal statements and proofs, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, of Helling's theorem and of consequences for normalizers. A subgroup G ≤ SL₂(ℝ) is commensurable with SL₂(ℤ) if G ∩ SL₂(ℤ) has finite index in G and in SL₂(ℤ); Γ₀(N)⁺ is the group generated by the Atkin–Lehner elements of level N, and contains Γ₀(N). Every G commensurable with SL₂(ℤ) is conjugate into Γ₀(N)⁺ for some squarefree N, by (det A)^{−1/2}·A for an integral matrix A with det A > 0. For every N ≥ 1, Γ₀(N)⁺ is commensurable with SL₂(ℤ), and for squarefree N it is maximal among such groups; so the maximal subgroups of SL₂(ℝ) commensurable with SL₂(ℤ) are the conjugates of the Γ₀(N)⁺, N squarefree, that are commensurable with SL₂(ℤ) (Duncan's Theorem 2.11, in SL₂(ℝ)), and Γ₀(4)⁺ is not maximal. The commensurator of SL₂(ℤ) in SL₂(ℝ) consists of the (det A)^{−1/2}·A. For every Γ commensurable with SL₂(ℤ), the normalizer of Γ in SL₂(ℝ) is commensurable with SL₂(ℤ), so Nor(Γ)/Γ is finite, and Nor(Γ) is conjugate into Γ₀(N)⁺ for some squarefree N. The proof is the argument with p-adic trees that Duncan attributes to Conway, with an integral matrix for each vertex and distances computed from p-adic valuations of determinants and of the gcd of the entries; the vertices and edges fixed at the different primes are glued with the Smith normal form. 9 theorems, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: Helling's theorem: the maximal subgroups of SL₂(ℝ) commensurable with SL₂(ℤ)

entries.abstract: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof, with no hypothesis, of Theorem 1, equation 11, of D. A. Goldston and A. I. Suriajaya, On an average Goldbach representation formula of Fujii, Nagoya Math. J. 250, 2023, 511 to 532, arXiv 2110.14250v2. With psi_2(n) the sum over m + m' = n of Lambda(m) Lambda(m'), for every integer N >= 2 the sum over n <= N of psi_2(n) equals N^2/2 - 2 times the sum over nontrivial zeros rho of N^{rho+1} divided by rho times rho+1, minus 2 log 2pi - 1/2 times N, plus 2 zeta'/zeta at -1, minus the sum over k >= 1 of N^{1-2k} divided by k times 2k-1, plus E(N), an exact identity with E(N) the integral of equation 12. The zero sum counts zeros with multiplicity. Derived results of this entry, not statements of the paper, show that E(N) does not depend on the radius r, that every term is real, that the zero sum converges absolutely, and the case N = 2. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed; this is an average over n. An AI agent wrote the Lean code; the statements were checked against the paper by an AI agent and are offered for human audit.
entries.title: An exact average Goldbach representation formula, after Goldston and Suriajaya

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of Ruzsa's lower bound for sumsets in ℝ^D: if A and B are finite sets with B nonempty and |B| ≤ |A|, and A + B has affine dimension d, then |A + B| ≥ |A| + Σ_{t=1}^{|B|-1} min(d, |A| - t). For d ≥ 1 and |A| ≥ d + 1 the bound is attained in ℝ^d. The closed form |A + B| ≥ |A| + d|B| - d(d+1)/2, the asymmetric form of Freiman's lemma, is derived from the bound, and so is the bound 2κ - 1, for a real κ, on the Freiman dimension of a set X with |X + X| ≤ κ|X|.
entries.title: Sum of sets in several dimensions

entries.abstract:
Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, about cut-and-project schemes on a fixed integer lattice Z^iota invariant under an integer matrix A: splittings R^iota = E + H into A-invariant subspaces with Z^iota meeting H only in 0 and the projection of Z^iota to H dense in H, a window W in H (bounded, containing a relative ball), the model set Lambda(W) = {pi_E g : g in Z^iota, pi_H g in W}, and admissibility, some window with A Lambda(W) contained in Lambda(W) (inflation symmetry in Meyer's inclusion sense). The least physical dimension d(A) is the least dim E over admissible schemes. Thirteen compared theorems. (1) For every integer A, a scheme is admissible iff A is power-bounded on H; then the orbit window is a compact convex symmetric invariant window; the per-window criterion; and U(A) <= dim E, U(A) the number of eigenvalues of modulus > 1. (2) Kronecker's density criterion in cut-and-project form. (3) For every integer A with det A != 0, any chi_A: (a) d(A) is the sum over the distinct irreducible factors p of chi_A over Q of m_p u_p + c_p (m_p - r_1(p)), plus min(deg p, 2) when every root of p lies on the unit circle and r_1(p) = m_p, where m_p is the multiplicity, u_p and c_p count the roots of p of modulus > 1 and = 1, and r_1(p) = (2 dim ker p(A) - dim ker p(A)^2) / deg p (ranks over Q) is the number of Jordan blocks of size one at each root of p; (b) the value is an invariant of rational similarity; (c) the factors with all roots on the unit circle are the cyclotomic ones; and (d) for chi_A squarefree every invariant splitting is E = ker q_E(A), H = ker q_H(A) with chi_A = q_E q_H, it is admissible iff the roots of q_H lie in the closed unit disk and every irreducible rational factor of chi_A shares a root with q_E, and d(A) = U(A) + circleCount(A), counting 1 for each factor x - 1, x + 1 and 2 for each other cyclotomic factor, each with its multiplicity. (4) For det A != 0 and hyperbolic A, any chi_A and no diagonalizability: a scheme is admissible iff E contains the unstable set iff H lies in the stable set; an invariant splitting carries an admissible scheme iff E contains the unstable set; d(A) = U(A), attained only by the unstable/stable splitting. (5) For det A != 0, any chi_A: d(A) = 1 iff chi_A is irreducible with exactly one root of modulus > 1 (a real root, a Pisot or Salem number up to sign, or an integer on Z^1), or A = +-1 in any rank; in the irreducible case every admissible line is the eigenline. (6) If A^k = 1: every factor is cyclotomic and d = sum of min(deg p, 2) over the distinct factors; the same for chi_A squarefree with all roots on the unit circle; every integer matrix with chi_A = Phi_n, n >= 3 (multiplication by a primitive n-th root of unity), needs exactly a plane. (7) Jordan blocks on the circle: I_2 and the Jordan block J_2 both have chi = (x - 1)^2, for which the squarefree count of (3), with x - 1 counted twice, gives 2, but d = 1 and 2; 1 + J_2(1) and 1 + J_3(1) have d = 2 and 3. (8) Multiplication by rho, rho^-1, Q and theta = -Q^-1 = 1 - Q^3 on Z[rho] and Z[Q] (rho^3 = rho + 1, Q^4 = Q + 1): d = 1, 2, 3, 1. (9) On Z[rho] (x) Z[Q] (degree 12), multiplication by every alpha other than 0, +-1 is nonsingular (det != 0) and hyperbolic with d = U; for rho, theta, rho Q and Q the values are 4, 3, 5, 9. (10) rho and theta act on their unstable spaces as real scalars, and the spectral projection carries the quartic (resp. cubic) sector onto them with the Gram pairing GramRho (x) GramQ equal to that of GramQ (resp. GramRho), of types (3,1) and (2,1). (11) The scheme of Q on Z^4 with an interval window: a segment, an explicit Q-invariant model set in R^3, determinant -1/q' on E, non-real moduli, and the types (2,1) and (1,0) of the trace form on E and H. (12) A Salem witness, the companion of x^4 - x^3 - x^2 - x + 1: not hyperbolic, d = 1. (13) Every model set is a Delone set (Mathlib's Delone.DeloneSet) with uniformly discrete difference set. The mathematics of (1), (2), (4), (5) for irreducible chi_A, and (13), and of (6) for chi_A = Phi_n, is known in other formulations (Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova 2021; Kronecker, Pleasants 2000; Harriss-Koivusalo-Walton 2025, preprint; Meyer 1972, 1995; Lagarias 1999; Solomyak 2020; the classical cyclotomic model sets; Moody 1997); (1) and (4) are stated with no diagonalizability hypothesis. The scheme and model set of (11) are, in substance, instances of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova Thm 13.1 and of Harriss-Koivusalo-Walton Section 3.4, and are not new. For squarefree chi_A the count of (3) also follows from the arguments of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova (Lemma 5.1, Prop. 8.1(iii), Cor. 13.4), stated there for generic (aperiodic) schemes; the lattice-first least physical dimension was not found stated in the sources read (search completed 2026-10-20). Beyond the cited cases, the entry proves the least physical dimension for every nonsingular integer matrix (3), including what lies outside the diagonalizable class of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova: a Jordan block of size >= 2 at an eigenvalue on the unit circle counts in full (the terms c_p (m_p - r_1(p)), which vanish for diagonalizable A), and at a cyclotomic factor with such a block the blocks of size one cost nothing, the internal space being tilted into the socle of the larger blocks; the witnesses are J_2, 1 + J_2(1) and 1 + J_3(1) (7). Every admissible scheme of an A with such a block at a root of unity has Z^iota meeting E in a nonzero vector. It also proves the characterization of every admissible splitting for squarefree chi_A ((3)(d)), non-generic splittings included (its necessity half is the injectivity argument of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova, Lemma 5.1), and (1) for every integer matrix and (4) for every nonsingular hyperbolic integer matrix, with no diagonalizability hypothesis; for diagonalizable A and generic schemes, the uniqueness of the minimal scheme in (4) and of the minimal physical line in (5) is immediate from Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova, Cor. 13.4. For det A != 0 and squarefree chi_A with a factor Phi_n, n not in {1, 2, 3, 4, 6}, the minimal scheme is not unique, by (3)(d). The companion matrices are multiplication by rho and Q in the power bases by definition, so Crho^i (x) CQ^j is multiplication by rho^i Q^j in the product basis. That the rho^i Q^j are a Z-basis of the ring of integers of Q(rho, Q) is statement (8) of the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012 (stalex444/pdt-hermite-signature-compositum@5aa870e98236ba240561b798265c629df8c2d031); that GramRho, GramQ and GramRho (x) GramQ are the Gram matrices of the trace forms in these bases is statements (8), (9) and (19) of the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014, in which Q(rho) (x) Q(Q) is the field Q(rho, Q) (its (23)). These are cited, not compared. Application (cited, not a claim of the entry): In the author's Pisot Dimensional Theory, Q(rho) is the arithmetic of three-dimensional space and Q(Q) the arithmetic of four-dimensional spacetime, and their compositum K, whose integers are Z[rho] (x) Z[Q], is the parent of both (the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012 (stalex444/pdt-hermite-signature-compositum@5aa870e98236ba240561b798265c629df8c2d031), statements (7), (8)). A model set is the shadow of a lattice cut through a window, a standard mathematical model of a quasicrystal (Moody 2000). Read through the theory, this entry's theorems fix how many dimensions each of the theory's inflations needs to be the symmetry of one, and which ones.
Space inflates the parent through spacetime, and spacetime inflates it through space. On the parent's lattice the plastic inflation rho needs exactly four physical dimensions, and only one scheme attains four (4, 9). Those four are a copy of spacetime's: rho has a single expanding embedding in Q(rho), the real one, and the spectral projection maps the quartic sector onto them, carrying Z[Q] with its trace form unchanged, of Lorentzian type (3,1) (10). rho acts on them as a pure dilation by rho = 1.3247..., the same stretch in every direction (10). Symmetrically, the unit theta = -Q^-1 = 1 - Q^3 needs exactly three, and those three are a copy of space's: Q(rho)'s real space with its form of type (2,1) unchanged, dilated by t = -1/q' = 1.3803... (8, 9, 10). Taken over all three embeddings of Q(rho) instead of the one expanding embedding, the form on the quartic sector is tripled: the factor 3 of statement (13) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012.
The clock needs one dimension; the ruler needs five. On Z[rho] the plastic inflation needs exactly one: the line, over a two-dimensional window at the complex place (8). The plastic substitution's control-point sets are regular model sets in this scheme, with Rauzy-fractal windows in C (Baake and Grimm 2020), and in the theory the line is time and its points are the ticks (PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006, PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019). The coupling ruler rho Q, which generates the parent field (Q(rho Q) = K; statement (15) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012, where Z[rho Q] has index 53 in the integers; PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005), needs exactly five, over a seven-dimensional window (9): one real and two complex expanding places, a dimension neither sector has.
The parent holds no circle, so every minimal scheme is forced. Off the parent, eigenvalues on the unit circle can change the count: a Salem inflation's circle eigendirections lie in the internal space and cost nothing, so it still needs only a line (5, 12), but multiplication by a primitive n-th root of unity, n >= 3, needs exactly a plane, and every element of finite order n >= 3 needs at least one (6). The parent has none. No element of K other than +-1 has a conjugate on the unit circle (statement (17) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012), so every inflation of the parent by an element other than 0 and +-1 is hyperbolic, needs exactly as many dimensions as it has expanding embeddings (a complex place counts twice), and has a unique minimal scheme (4, 9).
entries.title: The least physical dimension of an inflation-symmetric model set, with the cubic, quartic and degree-12 inflations of x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of the main result of the preprint "Szemerédi's theorem with random differences and arithmetic Kakeya" by Gabriel Dahia (arXiv:2610.18859), a threshold for Szemerédi's theorem with random differences. For c = 1/100, k ≥ 3, δ > 0 and p ≥ C n^(-c / log log k), where C is a value of the Ackermann function depending on k and δ, a p-random set D of differences in {1, …, n} has the following property with probability at least 1 - exp(-n^(1 - c / log log k)): every subset of {1, …, n} with at least δn elements contains a k-term arithmetic progression with common difference in D. The proof uses the Green–Ruzsa construction of small sets containing a progression with every common difference, which is also formalized.
entries.title: Szemerédi's theorem with random differences

entries.abstract: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof of Renyi's theorem: there is N0 such that every even N >= N0 is p + m with p prime, m >= 1 and Omega of m at most 8, where Omega counts prime factors with multiplicity, as Mathlib's ArithmeticFunction.cardFactors does. So the theorem is proved with the explicit constant K = 8. Also proved: a lower bound e^{-36} N / 2 log^2 N for the number of primes p < N with Omega of N - p at most 8; the same two statements with the weaker K = 13000; and the K = 8 statement written with Mathlib's Nat.IsAtMostAlmostPrime. The entry also proves twin_renyi_count, a derived analogue proved in this entry by the same sieve method, a twin-prime analogue of Renyi's theorem, not a result of Renyi 1948. The proof is a Brun type block sieve with Bonferroni levels whose remainders are bounded by the Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem proved in the same library; all thresholds are ineffective through Siegel's theorem. Nothing here is new mathematics: Pan has K = 4 and Chen 1973 has K = 2. Binary Goldbach is Omega of m equal to 1; it is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent; the statements were checked against the literature by AI reviewers and are offered for human audit.
entries.title: Renyi's theorem, Renyi 1948: every large even number is a prime plus a number with at most 8 prime factors

entries.abstract: We prove a uniform all-cardinality existence theorem for noncrossing chronological two-nearest-predecessor graphs on sufficiently near-circular ellipses. Put R = sqrt(2/sin(2*pi/5) - 1). For every ellipse with semiaxes a >= b > 0 and a/b <= R, and every finite set of at least three distinct boundary sites, there is an order starting with a triangle in which every subsequent site is joined to exactly its two Euclidean-nearest earlier sites. All edges persist, and no two independent edges properly cross. Cartesian-lexicographic order resolves equal-distance predecessor ties. The sufficient ratio bound includes equality, all finite cardinalities and arbitrarily close distinct sites. The interest lies in planarity despite compulsory distance-ranked edges: unlike conventional convex-polygon triangulation, the two incoming edges cannot be chosen just to avoid crossings. The constructive proof uses recursive metric-ear deletion; the accompanying manuscript also gives an exact-real comparison-model algorithm, whose complexity is not a separately compared Lean claim. The bound is not claimed to be sharp; historical priority remains unestablished. The repository also contains formally proved supporting geometry and a concrete noncircular corollary, but these are not submitted as independent research results in the selected Comparator configuration.
entries.title: Noncrossing Two-Nearest-Predecessor Orders on Nearly Circular Ellipses

entries.abstract: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof of the Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem in its classical form: for every A > 0 there is B > 0 such that the sum over q <= x^{1/2} (log x)^{-B} of the maximum over y <= x and over reduced residues a mod q of |psi(y; q, a) - y/phi(q)| is << x (log x)^{-A}. The same form is proved for theta(y; q, a), for pi(y; q, a) against liD(y)/phi(q) with liD(y) the sum of 1/log n over 2 <= n <= y, and for pi(y; q, a) against pi(y)/phi(q), the level of distribution 1/2 input of sieve methods. The proof runs from a zero-free region for Dirichlet L-functions and Siegel's theorem through the Siegel-Walfisz theorem, the multiplicative large sieve and Vaughan's identity; all constants are ineffective, as in the papers. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent; the statements were checked against the literature by AI reviewers and are offered for human audit.
entries.title: The Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem, Bombieri 1965 and A. I. Vinogradov 1965, classical form with the maximum over y <= x

entries.abstract: Conditional on RH: a sorry-free Lean 4 proof of Theorem 1 of A. Languasco and A. Zaccagnini, The number of Goldbach representations of an integer, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 140 2012, 795 to 804. With G(n) the sum over m1 + m2 = n of Lambda(m1) Lambda(m2), Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis, taken as an explicit hypothesis of the theorem and never as an axiom, implies that the sum over n <= N of G(n) equals N^2/2 - 2 times the sum over nontrivial zeros rho of N^{rho+1} divided by rho times rho+1, plus O(N log^3 N), for N >= 2. The weaker earlier error terms of Fujii, O((N log N)^{4/3}), and of Bhowmik and Schlage-Puchta, O(N log^5 N), follow and are stated too. The zero sum counts zeros with multiplicity, and its absolute convergence is proved unconditionally. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed; this is an average over n. An AI agent wrote the Lean code; the statements were checked against the papers by an AI agent and are offered for human audit.
entries.title: Conditional on RH: the number of Goldbach representations on average, after Languasco and Zaccagnini

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps, of the theorem of H. B. Mann, A proof of the fundamental theorem on the density of sums of sets of positive integers, Ann. of Math. 43, 1942: for sets A and B of natural numbers that contain 0, the Schnirelmann density of A + B is at least the minimum of 1 and sigma A + sigma B. It is stated for Mathlib's own schnirelmannDensity and Mathlib's pointwise sum of sets, so the Challenge restates no density definition, and it is also proved for any finite number of sets. This fills a Mathlib TODO: Mathlib/Combinatorics/Schnirelmann.lean lists Mann's theorem as not yet proved. The proof goes through the rank h case of Dyson's theorem, following Nathanson, arXiv 2407.12253. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent and is offered for human audit.
entries.title: Mann's alpha plus beta theorem for Schnirelmann density, after Mann 1942

entries.abstract: Conditional on RH: a sorry-free Lean 4 proof of Theorem 2 of D. A. Goldston and L. Yang, The average number of Goldbach representations, arXiv 1601.06902, in Prime numbers and representation theory, Science Press 2017. With G(n) the sum over m1 + m2 = n of Lambda(m1) Lambda(m2), Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis, taken as an explicit hypothesis of the theorem and never as an axiom, implies that the sum over n <= N of 1 - n/N times G(n) equals N^2/6 - 2 times the sum over nontrivial zeros rho of N^{rho+1} divided by rho times rho+1 times rho+2, plus O(N), for N >= 2. The zero sum counts zeros with multiplicity, and its absolute convergence is proved unconditionally. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed; this is an average over n. An AI agent wrote the Lean code; the statements were checked against the paper by an AI agent and are offered for human audit.
entries.title: Conditional on RH: the Cesàro average of the number of Goldbach representations, after Goldston and Yang

entries.abstract: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof, with no hypothesis, of Theorems B, C, D, E and F of G. H. Hardy and J. E. Littlewood, Some problems of Partitio Numerorum III, Acta Math. 44, 1923. Hardy and Littlewood proved these theorems on their Hypothesis R, a form of the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions; here they are proved unconditionally, from Vinogradov's estimate for exponential sums over primes and the Siegel-Walfisz theorem, so the argument is not Hardy and Littlewood's own for Theorems B, D and E. Formalized: Theorem B, the asymptotic for the weighted count nu_r of n as an ordered sum of r primes, for every r at least 3 and n of the parity of r, with the singular series written as the paper's product over the odd primes dividing n, and nu_r of n is o of n^{r-1} for unlike parity; Theorem C, N_r of n is asymptotic to nu_r of n over log^r n; Theorem D, the ternary asymptotic with the constant C_3 and every large odd number a sum of three odd primes; Theorem E, the asymptotic for four odd primes, every large even number a sum of four odd primes, one of which may be assigned; and Theorem F, that an asymptotic of Conjecture A's shape for binary Goldbach can only carry the constant 2 C_2, together with a check that the printed formula 4.23 has a misprint. Theorem A of the paper is not formalized. Ternary Goldbach is Helfgott's theorem; binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent; the statements were written from the paper's page images by AI agents and are offered for human audit.
entries.title: Sums of primes, after Hardy and Littlewood 1923, Partitio Numerorum III, Theorems B to F proved without Hypothesis R

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of H. Iwaniec, "On the error term in the linear sieve" (Acta Arith. 19, 1971) and "On the problem of Jacobsthal" (Demonstratio Math. 11, 1978). The headline result is Iwaniec's bound for Jacobsthal's problem: if m consecutive integers are each divisible by one of r ≥ 2 given primes, then m ≤ C (r log r)² for an absolute constant C. More strongly, every interval of length c ∏ (1 − 1/q)⁻¹ r² log r contains at least r² integers coprime to r given primes. Both the Theorem and the Corollary of the 1978 paper are proved, together with its Lemma 1 (the shifted sieve, both bounds) and Lemma 2. The 1971 paper is formalized in full: the Rosser–Iwaniec linear sieve at the sifting limit with general modulus k and arbitrary finite sequences (§2); the sieve functions f, F and the majorants 𝔐, 𝔚 defined by delay-differential equations, including F(3) = 2e^γ − 3 and the asymptotics of 𝔐 (§3); the main term with error O(1/log y) and support of size O(y / log² y) (§4, Theorems 4 and 5); and Theorem 1 with its Corollary, Theorem 2 (C₀(r) ≪ r² log² r) and Theorem 3 (§5). The prime number theorem with de la Vallée Poussin error term and Mertens' theorems come from a vendored copy of PrimeNumberTheoremAnd.
entries.title: Iwaniec's linear sieve at the sifting limit and Jacobsthal's problem

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of Shelah's proof of the Hales–Jewett theorem. For k ≥ 1 letters and r colors, every coloring with r colors of the words of length n over k letters has a monochromatic combinatorial line when n is at least the Ackermann function at level 5 and argument 2k + r.
entries.title: Shelah's bound for the Hales–Jewett numbers

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorems 1, 2 and 3 of Duminil-Copin, Sidoravicius and Tassion (arXiv:1505.04159v1). Theorem 3: for the random-cluster model on the square lattice with any real cluster weight q >= 1, at its critical point p_c, the following are equivalent: the origin lies in an infinite cluster with probability 0 under the wired measure; equality of the free and wired measures; infinite susceptibility of the free measure; sub-exponential decay of the free one-arm probability; and the RSW bound for free boundary conditions at distance n. Theorem 2: for 1 <= q <= 4 the wired measure at p_c gives probability 0 to the origin lying in an infinite cluster. Theorem 1: for the q-state Potts model with q = 2, 3, 4, the monochromatic Gibbs measure at beta_c gives its own colour at the origin probability exactly 1/q, so the phase transition is continuous. The critical points are the genuine phase-transition thresholds, whose existence the theorems assert; four further theorems prove that these critical points and the infinite-volume measures are unique; beyond this statement surface, the development also proves p_c = sqrt(q)/(1 + sqrt q) for every q >= 1 (PottsContinuity.BD12.isRCCriticalPoint_sqrt) and beta_c = log(1 + sqrt q) for every integer q >= 2 (PottsContinuity.Thm1.isPottsCriticalPoint_log_sqrt); these identifications are not checked by Comparator. The infinite-volume measures are limits along every exhaustion of the lattice, and their existence and uniqueness are proved. The external results that the paper cites and the proof uses (the value of p_c and the crossing estimates of Beffara-Duminil-Copin, the contour identity of the parafermionic observable in the form used in Section 4 of the paper, Theorem 4 of the paper, the Edwards-Sokal coupling, FKG and comparison inequalities, the domain Markov property, planar duality and topology) are proved here or taken from Mathlib; the Jordan-Schoenflies theorem and Brouwer's fixed-point theorem come from vendored libraries, and circle-degree and Jordan-curve facts from the Tau Ceti library. The only axioms are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: Continuity of the phase transition for planar random-cluster and Potts models with 1 <= q <= 4 (Theorems 1, 2 and 3)

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 formalization of Jeffrey Shallit and Jonathan Sorenson, "Analysis of a Left-Shift Binary GCD Algorithm" (J. Symbolic Computation 17, 1994). LSBGCD replaces (u, v) by v and the distance from u to the nearer of the shifted multiples 2^e v and 2^(e+1) v, where 2^e v ≤ u < 2^(e+1) v. The formalization proves that the algorithm computes the gcd, and proves Theorem 1.1: for every n, the lexicographically least ordered input taking exactly n iterations, its six closed forms in powers of 2 ± √3, and the order-16 linear recurrence satisfied by both coordinates. It proves in full generality Ramharter's theorem on continuant-minimising permutations (Theorem 5.1, quoted in the paper from Ramharter 1983), for arbitrary positive digits with repetition and with uniqueness up to reversal. It also proves the paper's binary minimiser classification (Theorem 5.2) and the sharp logarithmic iteration bound of §7 with an explicit additive constant. In addition it proves the sum-of-squares conjecture stated without proof at the end of §6: for n ≥ 2, among ordered positive inputs taking exactly n iterations, u² + v² is uniquely minimised by consecutive terms of the printed recurrence, which are denominators of convergents to √3. A limited literature search found no earlier proof of this conjecture, but its novelty has not been established.
entries.title: Analysis of a left-shift binary GCD algorithm (Shallit–Sorenson 1994), with a proof of its sum-of-squares conjecture

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the main vector bound, the explicit set-family bound, and the no-prefactor conjecture in Proof of the Erdős-Szemerédi sunflower conjecture by Matija Bucić, Fankang He, and Hyunwoo Lee (arXiv:2610.26686). The complete proof development uses Mathlib and contains no unresolved proof holes or nonstandard axioms.
entries.title: The Erdős–Szemerédi sunflower conjecture

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalisation of the main results of Castryck, Cluckers, Dittmann and Nguyen, "The dimension growth conjecture, polynomial in the degree and without logarithmic factors" (Algebra & Number Theory 14, 2020), incorporating the authors' 2026 addenda. It proves uniform bounds, polynomial in the degree, for the number of rational points of bounded height on varieties over Q. The bounds are: projective dimension growth N(X,B) ≤ C(n) d^(2n²+5n−5) B^dim X for integral X ⊆ P^n of degree d ≥ 5 (Theorem 1); N(X,B) ≤ C(n) d⁴ B^(2/d) for integral projective curves (Theorem 2); N_aff(X,B) ≤ C(n) d³ B^(1/d)(log B + d) for integral affine curves (Theorem 3); and C(N) d^(3N+9) B^(N−2) for affine hypersurfaces whose top-degree form is absolutely irreducible (Theorem 4). It also proves the lower-bound construction d² B^(2/d)/5 (Proposition 5), and the 2-torsion bound h₂(K) ≤ C(n) |disc K|^(1/2−1/(2n)) (log |disc K|)^(1−n mod 2) for all number fields of degree n ≥ 3 (Theorem 6). Degree and dimension are defined through Hilbert functions of the coordinate ring. Every constant depends only on the ambient dimension or field degree. The proofs construct the paper's determinant-method, projection and counting arguments in full. They include corrected versions of several intermediate lemmas whose printed forms are false.
entries.title: Dimension growth, polynomial in the degree (Castryck–Cluckers–Dittmann–Nguyen)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the characterization of Hamiltonian paths in rectangular grid graphs by Itai, Papadimitriou and Szwarcfiter (1982, Theorem 3.2). For distinct vertices s and t of the width × height grid graph, a Hamiltonian path from s to t exists if and only if the problem is acceptable, that is, colour compatible (by the checkerboard colouring) and not one of the three forbidden configurations F1, F2, F3 on grids of width or height 1, 2 or 3. Necessity is proved for each forbidden case, where the paper only says "a straightforward case analysis". Sufficiency is proved by strong induction with an explicit reduction rule (strip two columns or split at a cut edge) and 596 kernel-checked base-case paths.
entries.title: Hamiltonian paths in rectangular grid graphs (Itai, Papadimitriou and Szwarcfiter)

entries.abstract: An unconditional Lean formalization of the authors' fixed-force anomalous-dissipation construction on the three-dimensional torus, including all-exponent regularity for the same velocity and pressure.
entries.title: Fixed-force anomalous dissipation

entries.abstract: An unconditional Lean proof of the strict inequality lambda_5 / lambda_4 < C_N for every nonempty bounded connected open subset of Euclidean space of dimension at least two, with variational Dirichlet eigenvalues and the sharp Bessel-zero constant. No boundary regularity is assumed.
entries.title: The fourth consecutive Dirichlet eigenvalue ratio

entries.abstract: Critical detecting-set counts, physical test-list and black-box query lower bounds, and critical-set and cycle recovery through a fixed source-reading program. Primal/incidence treewidth bounds concern specification and complete binary-expanded native CNF graphs; a conditional cover-layout theorem bounds treewidth, net-cutwidth and block width. Strong and deletion backdoors into Horn, renamable-Horn and two-CNF have cardinality at least the bus count for both native and specification formulas.
entries.title: Critical recovery, query lower bounds and binary-native width

entries.abstract: Lean 4 proof that there exists a presentation with two generators and thirteen relators whose group contains an isomorphic copy of every finitely presented group. The construction combines a universal finitely presented input, positive preparation, word recognition, a six-generator nineteen-relator host, and a final HNN compression.
entries.title: A universal group with thirteen relators

entries.title: A formal proof that crown graphs maximise the representation number of bipartite graphs

entries.abstract: For the classical Liénard system dx/dt = y − F(x), dy/dt = −x, every polynomial in an explicit coefficient box of radius 10^−40 around a rational sextic has at least six limit cycles. For every integer n ≥ 6, a real polynomial of degree exactly n with F(0) = 0 is shown to have at least floor((n − 1)/2) + 4 limit cycles. An explicit rational polynomial of degree seven, obtained by adding 10^−41 x^7 to the sextic, has at least seven limit cycles. The conclusions provide global nonconstant periodic solutions with pairwise disjoint images, prescribed positive-axis crossings and isolating neighborhoods for the same periodic orbits. The construction combines rational integration certificates, half-return maps and a degree-raising argument.
entries.title: Classical Liénard equations of degree n ≥ 6 can have floor((n−1)/2)+4 limit cycles

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of modular forms over coefficient subrings of the complex numbers, their coefficientwise reductions modulo ring homomorphisms,  and a proof classifying the Ramanujan congruences for the partition function following an argument from Ahlgren and Boylan.  The recorded results prove Ramanujan's congruences modulo 5, 7, and 11  as well as the fact there there are no other such examples. The proof develops modular forms modulo a prime, filtration, and theta and U operators, using the arguments of Ahlgren–Boylan, Kiming–Olsson, and Swinnerton-Dyer.
entries.title: Ramanujan congruences for the partition function

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Theorem 1 of "Maximum-weight independent set in embedded graphs parameterized by Euler genus and number of odd faces" (forthcoming), with a provably correct implementation of the algorithm as one fixed program for an explicit sixteen-register pointer machine. Lean proves that for every graph drawn in a closed surface of Euler genus gamma whose complement has k regions of odd total boundary length, and all rational vertex weights, the program outputs a maximum-weight independent set within f(gamma + k) * N^(D(gamma, k) + C) * (L + 1)^b bit operations, with D(gamma, k) = max {0, gamma + k - 2, gamma - 1}, improved to max {0, gamma + k - 2} on orientable surfaces; f is an explicit computable function and C, b are absolute constants. Surfaces are represented by finite combinatorial flag maps; disconnected and noncellular drawings, loops, multiple edges, isolated vertices and negative weights are covered. The cost is a logarithmic bit-cost measure including an explicit stack simulation of recursive calls. The proofs use exactly propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: An XP Algorithm for Maximum-Weight Independent Set in Embedded Graphs, in Lean 4

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps, of the theorem of L. Schnirelmann, Über additive Eigenschaften von Zahlen, Math. Ann. 107, 1933: the set of 0, 1 and the sums of two primes has positive Schnirelmann density, and so every integer n >= 2 is a sum of a bounded number of primes. The proof also gives an explicit bound: every n >= 2 is a sum of at most 30772 primes. Mathlib's file Mathlib/Combinatorics/Schnirelmann.lean lists the proof of Schnirelmann's theorem as a TODO; this entry gives it, for Mathlib's schnirelmannDensity, with an explicit constant. The constant 30772 is far weaker than the best known ones: Ramaré 1995 showed that every n >= 2 is a sum of at most 7 primes, and Helfgott's ternary Goldbach theorem gives at most 4. The point is a complete formal version of Schnirelmann's argument with every constant explicit. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent and is offered for human audit.
entries.title: Schnirelmann's theorem: every integer n >= 2 is a sum of at most 30772 primes, after Schnirelmann 1933

entries.abstract: A Lean proof that every finite t-perfect graph is 50-colorable. Here t-perfection means equality between the stable set polytope and the polytope described by coordinate, edge, and odd-cycle inequalities.
entries.title: The 50-color theorem for t-perfect graphs

entries.abstract: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof of the theorem of V. Brun, La série 1/5 + 1/7 + 1/11 + 1/13 + ... où les dénominateurs sont nombres premiers jumeaux est convergente ou finie, Bull. Sci. Math. 43, 1919: the sum of the reciprocals of p and of p + 2 over the primes p with p + 2 prime converges. This is a sorry-free proof of a statement that lean-eval lists as a challenge, brun_constant_converges, proved here in the exact lean-eval form as well. With it, the twin prime upper bound, at most C N / log^2 N twin primes below N, which is stronger than the bound of Brun's paper; the same convergence for prime pairs p, p + h with any even gap h; a bound for those pairs with one constant for every gap; and its average over gaps. The bounds come from the Selberg sieve, ported from PrimeNumberTheoremAnd, not from Brun's sieve. Binary Goldbach and the twin prime conjecture are open and are not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent and is offered for human audit.
entries.title: Brun's theorem: the sum of the reciprocals of the twin primes converges, after Brun 1919, with the twin prime upper bound and every even gap

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps, of the theorem of N. P. Romanov, Über einige Sätze der additiven Zahlentheorie, Math. Ann. 109, 1934: the integers p + 2^k, p prime, have positive lower density, for k >= 0 and for k >= 1. With it, the result of P. Erdős, On integers of the form 2^k + p and some related problems, Summa Brasil. Math. 2, 1950: by a covering system, every 119477317 + 346729110 t is odd and is not p + 2^k, so the odd numbers that are not of that form also have positive lower density. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent and is offered for human audit.
entries.title: Romanov's theorem: the integers of the form p + 2^k have positive lower density, with Erdős' complement, after Romanov 1934 and Erdős 1950

entries.abstract: For every second-countable metrizable topological space, the second player has a winning full-history strong Choquet strategy if and only if the topology admits a complete metric, equivalently if and only if the space is Polish. Moves include a marked point which every response must retain. The difficult converse constructs a coherent countable response tree, proves the embedded image is Gδ, and transfers complete metrizability from the metric completion. Supporting results prove complete-metric winning strategies without second countability, complete metrizability of Gδ subsets of arbitrary complete metric spaces, actual legal-play existence and explicit empty-space behavior. This is classical mathematics; no novelty or priority is claimed.

entries.abstract: Lean formalization of five manuscript result groups: Theorems 1.1, 1.3, and 1.6, and Corollaries 1.2 and 1.7. The upper bound is the continuous-time statement for every fixed exponent saving between zero and one quarter. The fluctuation exponents and mean-bias lower bound have their stated positive exponent slack. Corollary 1.7 also explicitly concludes convergence of the finite-volume counting pressures to the limiting pressure. The manuscript and exact scope are included.

entries.abstract: Let k be a field of characteristic zero and U a simple, infinite-dimensional k-algebra with an exhaustive nonnegative multiplicative filtration by finite-dimensional k-subspaces. Suppose F_0 U = k and the associated graded algebra is a commutative affine domain of finite Krull dimension. Then for every nonzero d, a in U and every B in U there exist H, R, S in U such that 1 = dR + (B + Ha)dS. The Lean 4 development proves this theorem, its left-handed form, and module generation, stable range and cancellation results for U.
entries.title: Symplectic Stafford: the affine same-divisor theorem

entries.abstract: Lean 4 proofs of the exact largest-Sidon-subset guarantee g(n)=ceil((n+1)/2) for finite weak Sidon sets, its asymptotic density 1/2, convergence and the optimal-constant characterization for finite (4,5)-sets, and the upper bound cStar<=4/7. The project also proves the finite three-uniform transversal bound 4tau<=n+m used in the exact guarantee. This is a partial formalization of Ma–Tang, arXiv:2602.23282v2: Theorem5.3 and the lower9/17 bound in Theorem1.6 remain unproved.
