entries.abstract: Exact supremum-operator norms for the undecimated periodic db2 cascade. For every level j and every period N at least the support, the norm is c_j^d, where c_j = 1651/1395 - (4/63)4^{-j} + (1/180)16^{-j} - (1/1736)32^{-j}. For every positive period, aliasing included, the norm is at most (1651/1395)^d, and that power is the least constant with this uniform role. The free mass is strictly increasing, converges to 1651/1395, and the gap is at most (4/63)4^{-j}. Dimension zero is exactly 1. N at least the support is sufficient, not claimed necessary, and one fixed period is not claimed to attain the limit. At dimension zero the least-constant conclusion is 1 ≤ B; it does not force B = 1. The level-one kernel is the seven-tap half-autocorrelation, with norm (9/8)^d for N >= 7. Levels 1, 2 and 3 remain the exact values (299/256)^d, (9663/8192)^d and (309991/262144)^d for N >= 19, 43 and 91. Bibliographic priority of the closed form is unresolved; see docs/RELATED_WORK.md. A conditional propagation then carries a supplied summary Lipschitz bound and a supplied seminorm comparison through the level-one operator. Bottleneck stability, persistence diagrams and landscape non-expansiveness are hypotheses, not theorems. Those conditional statements are retained in the sources as auxiliaries and are not selected. Nineteen statements are selected. They are parts of this development, not nineteen independent contributions. The exposition of the cascade argument is docs/CASCADE_THEOREM.md.
entries.title: Exact db2 cascade norms and an optimal uniform constant

entries.abstract: For arbitrary T1 omega-bounded factors with an explicit product basepoint, the countable-support Sigma-product is omega-bounded and countably compact. Every countable family is trapped, together with its ambient closure, in a closed compact coordinate box using one countable support. For compact Hausdorff factors, the Sigma-product is compact if and only if only countably many factors contain a point different from the basepoint. Uncountable discrete Boolean Sigma-products are countably compact but not compact. The index and factor universes are independent; the empty index and empty countable subsets are allowed. No first-countability or separability premise is added.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Omega-bounded Sigma-products and a sharp compactness criterion

entries.abstract: Survival and transience are established throughout the strictly supercritical regime of the noncoagulating compartment model of Anderson, Howells and Rojas La Luz (https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.10223v4, Remark 4.8). Compartments produce molecules at rate b, degrade them at rate d per molecule, exit at rate e, and divide at rate f per molecule, with arbitrary conservative allocation between the daughters. For b,e,f > 0 and d >= 0 with bf > e(e+d), every finite nonempty family has positive probability of eternal survival, with an explicit product lower bound. For positive immigration intensity and any distribution of finite immigrant contents, the process is nonexplosive and the expected total physical occupation time of every compartment-count state has an explicit finite bound. This establishes the transience conjectured in Remark 4.8 without a moment assumption on immigrant contents. The quantitative bounds use a positive eigenweight of the mean system and a bounded multiplicative barrier; a distribution-dependent immigration constant sharpens the uniform occupation bound.
entries.title: Survival and transience above the compartment-division threshold

entries.abstract: Formalization of a finite algebraic classification of approximate, approximate null, exact null, and exact controllability for finite-dimensional linear stochastic systems with constant coefficients and independent Brownian drivers. A decreasing subspace sequence gives a common obstruction for the first three properties; exact controllability additionally requires full row rank of the stacked diffusion-control matrix. The development also covers stochastic integration, forward and backward equations, duality, finite rank tests, null feedback, and polynomial small-time energy bounds. The independent Palomar statement and its solution compile with Lean v4.35.0-rc2 and canonical Mathlib. Complete sandboxed mechanical preflight and editorial review are separate requirements; no registration is claimed.
entries.title: A Unified Kalman-Type Classification of Controllability for Linear Stochastic Systems

entries.abstract: A computable algorithm, decideHamPath, that decides whether a solid grid graph (a finite set of lattice points with no holes, with an edge between points at distance 1) has a Hamiltonian path between two given distinct points, with a Lean 4 proof that it is correct. The problem was posed by Itai, Papadimitriou and Szwarcfiter (1982). The algorithm extends Sheffield's height-function algorithm for Hamiltonian cycles: each endpoint gets a phantom edge to a missing neighbour, and an endpoint with all eight neighbours present becomes a hole whose defect (a vortex) is handled by a slit height and a search over flip classes. The registered statement is correctness. The library also proves a polynomial step bound, 5 220 000 (|V| + 3)^6, for cost functions written beside the algorithm, and formalizes the Umans–Lenhart algorithm for Hamiltonian cycles in solid grid graphs.
entries.title: Hamiltonian s–t paths in solid grid graphs are decidable in polynomial time

entries.abstract: An explicit rational homogeneous cubic with 25 monomials in 14 real variables has maximum one on the Euclidean unit sphere and admits a positive degree-four moment functional with value 500753357629/500000000000. For every positive real regularization parameter, quadratic strength and cubic strength, the associated quartic has an explicitly attained global minimum whose shift is not a sum of squares of real polynomials. A quantitative strict separation bounds every SOS lower bound. The polynomial is stationary at zero with negative definite Hessian. A second explicit 25-term cubic, certified by the same rational functional, gives a unique global minimizer with positive-definite Hessian there and persistent SOS failure for all positive parameters. The exact sphere maximizers are classified. The proof combines an elementary quadratic-map contraction, a rational moment certificate, an ordinary SOS degree bound and an all-parameter radial factorization.
entries.title: Persistent failure of Euclidean quartic SOS exactness

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Galvin's theorem that the list chromatic index of a finite bipartite graph equals its maximum degree (if every edge has a list of at least Δ colours, a proper edge colouring can be chosen from the lists), of its corollary solving the Dinitz problem (an n × n array with lists of n symbols per cell admits a choice with distinct symbols in every row and column), and of the Gale–Shapley theorem on the existence of stable matchings with strict preferences and incomplete acceptability lists, which provides the kernels in Galvin's argument. Mathlib has line graphs and colourings but none of these results.
entries.title: Galvin's theorem, the Dinitz problem and stable matchings

entries.abstract: Formalizes the corrected construction of pure infinitely self-modifying code from Gregory Morse's 2018 paper. An unbounded integer-address machine simulates finite Turing machines, preserves halting and divergence, writes code at every computational instruction, and admits a run changing unboundedly many fetched code fields from a literal identity-memory initializer whose memory is proved primitive recursive. Terminal interpreter journals occur on reached halted configurations of the numbered interpreter on the encoded finite input. The development includes a four-register MOV foundation, effective finite-machine interpretation, tape and head observations, and conditional bounded x86/x64 instruction, relocation and native-trace refinements. Finite hardware is not claimed to have unbounded memory.
entries.title: Pure infinitely self-modifying code

entries.abstract: This repository introduces and formally proves the lower bound 4/3 for the limit inferior of the supremal hyperbolic systole in genus g divided by log g. At present, this formalization is the theorem's only public statement and proof. This metadata records the result as an original proof; the published papers below are cited only as background for ingredients. The proof combines arithmetic hyperbolic surfaces, uniform representations by comparable prime cubes, and surface gluing followed by a smooth conformal change to curvature minus one that preserves the systole lower bound.
entries.title: Systolic growth in every genus

entries.abstract: Every locally finite indexed family of arbitrary subsets of a paracompact topological space admits a locally finite open expansion with the same index type, without separation assumptions. In a paracompact normal space, a discrete closed family admits a discrete locally finite open expansion whose closures are pairwise disjoint and lie in prescribed open neighborhoods. Consequently every paracompact Hausdorff space is collectionwise normal. Index and ambient types may be empty and have independent universes; the family has unrestricted cardinality. These are classical results; no novelty is claimed.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Paracompact expansion and collectionwise separation

entries.abstract: This is a Lean 4 formalization of the pointwise a.e. convergence theorem for ergodic averages with respect to two commuting transformations. This theorem was proved by GPT 6 Pro when it was instructed to adapt the recent breakthrough on the triangular Hilbert transform made public by OpenAI. The formalization was generated by Claude Opus 5.5 Medium.
entries.title: Pointwise a.e. convergence of ergodic averages with respect to two commuting transformations in Lean

entries.abstract: Formalization of Theorem 1 (the Gromov–Milman conjecture on polynomials restricted to subspaces) from Dol'nikov–Karasev, "Dvoretzky type theorems for multivariate polynomials and sections of convex bodies" (arXiv:1009.0392): for any even d > 0 and any k, there exists n(d, k) such that every homogeneous polynomial of degree d on R^n (n >= n(d, k)) restricts on some k-dimensional subspace V to a scalar multiple of (x_1^2 + ... + x_n^2)^(d/2). The formalization provides an unconditional, constructive proof without sorry or external topological black boxes: Carlsson's theorem on non-abelian 2-groups is eliminated in favor of an elementary abelian Dold-type Borsuk–Ulam theorem ((Z/2)^r) proved from scratch on chain complexes and applied inductively level-by-level to iterated wreath products via block-structured join embeddings.
entries.title: GromovMilman

entries.abstract: A substantive Lean development of two-leg identifiability under independent relay deletion and nearest-surviving-ancestor bypass. An interior path sensor observes anonymous counts at each contracted hop, superimposing both legs. For every known real survival probability strictly between zero and one, the mean and covariance identify the unordered pair of natural-valued leg populations. A sparse interface needs only the covariance diagonal and one adaptively selected column. The concrete law is a finite sum over independent Bernoulli relay masks. Ten selected statements additionally establish mean/fold equivalence, endpoint trace and degenerate-probability semantics, actual-model variance bounds, conditional integer reconstruction recurrences, and a logarithmic randomized-testing lower bound for actual paths of every length at least two. The full finite-sample probability guarantee is not claimed.
entries.title: Lossy Distance-Shell Tomography on Paths: Recovery from Mean and Covariance

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Robbins' theorem: a finite connected simple graph has a strongly connected orientation (a digraph with underlying graph G, never containing both u → v and v → u, in which every vertex reaches every other) if and only if no edge of it is a bridge. As a corollary, every finite 2-edge-connected graph on a nonempty vertex type has a strongly connected orientation. Mathlib has bridges, edge connectivity and digraphs, but not this theorem.
entries.title: Robbins' theorem on strongly connected orientations

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 development of Graham's two bounds for scheduling independent jobs on identical machines to minimize the makespan (R. L. Graham, Bounds for certain multiprocessing anomalies, Bell System Tech. J. 45 (1966) 1563-1581; Bounds on multiprocessing timing anomalies, SIAM J. Appl. Math. 17 (1969) 416-429; both restated with their examples in his survey Bounds on multiprocessing anomalies and related packing algorithms, AFIPS Spring Joint Computer Conference (1972) 205-217). n jobs of nonnegative real lengths p : Fin n -> R are run without interruption on m >= 1 identical machines; an assignment sigma : Fin n -> Fin m loads machine i with the sum of the lengths assigned to it, its makespan is the largest load, and optMakespan m p is the least makespan over all m^n assignments. A list schedule (IsListSchedule, in the index order) gives each job a machine whose load from the earlier jobs is least, under any tie-breaking (a relation, so every theorem covers every tie-breaking); an LPT schedule (IsLPTSchedule) is a list schedule of the jobs in some nonincreasing order of length. Theorems, kernel-only: every list schedule sigma and every assignment tau satisfy m * C(sigma) <= (2m - 1) * C(tau) (Graham 1966, his Theorem for the same number of processors and no precedence constraints), so C(sigma) <= (2 - 1/m) * optMakespan; the m(m - 1) unit jobs followed by one job of length m (Graham's example for his theorem on scheduling the k largest tasks optimally first, at k = 0, as his 1972 survey restates it; Lenstra-Shmoys, Chapter 9, p. 188) have optimum m and every list schedule of them in that order has makespan 2m - 1, so 2 - 1/m is the least constant (IsLeast); every LPT schedule sigma and every assignment tau satisfy 3m * C(sigma) <= (4m - 1) * C(tau) (Graham 1969, Theorem 2, announced in the closing remarks of the 1966 paper), so C(sigma) <= (4/3 - 1/(3m)) * optMakespan; when every job is longer than a third of C(tau), every LPT schedule is at least as good as tau, so LPT is optimal when every job exceeds a third of the optimum; Graham's 2m + 1 jobs 2m - 1, 2m - 1, 2m - 2, 2m - 2, ..., m + 1, m + 1, m, m, m (his pp. 425-426) are in nonincreasing order, have optimum 3m, attained by a list schedule in the order 2m - 1, ..., m + 1, m, m, 2m - 1, ..., m + 1, m (the definition grahamOrder, a permutation of the jobs whose lengths are that list), and every LPT schedule of them has makespan 4m - 1, for every m >= 1, so 4/3 - 1/(3m) is the least constant (IsLeast); and the elementary facts (list and LPT schedules exist, the optimum is attained, every load, every job and the average load are at most the makespan, relabeling the jobs preserves the makespan); Graham's omega_0, the least finishing time over all lists, equals the optimum over all assignments (every assignment is matched or improved by a list schedule in some order), so the bounds against every assignment are his; for his instance the optimum is attained by an explicit list (grahamOrder); and the third of the optimality theorem cannot be weakened (on three machines 9, 5, 5, 4, 4, 4, each job at least a third of the optimum 12, has an LPT schedule of makespan 13, so n <= 2m jobs do not make LPT optimal; Graham's 1972 survey prints Spencer's 6, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2 for the same purpose); and the position of a job on its machine: the (c + 1)-th job k placed on a machine of a list schedule of a nonincreasing p has (c + 1) p_k <= C(tau) for every assignment tau (the property of Chen 1993, as Della Croce-Scatamacchia 2020 restate it; proved here by an invariant on pairs of machines), hence the Coffman-Sethi form q m C(sigma) <= ((q + 1) m - 1) C(tau) for a machine with q jobs attaining the makespan of an LPT schedule (Coffman-Sethi 1976 as corrected by Chen 1993, as Della Croce-Scatamacchia restate it; the literature states it for q >= 3, for m >= 2 it is weaker than the 4/3 - 1/(3m) bound at q <= 2, and neither its attainment nor Chen's 4/3 - 1/(3(m - 1)) at q = 2 is proved here; Chen's and Coffman-Sethi's papers were not read). The proof of the LPT bound is by counting, not by his exchange argument: with k the job ending a heaviest machine, the average-load bound settles 3 p_k <= C(tau), and otherwise a count of the jobs up to k (every machine of tau holds at most two of them, those at least as long as the least load sit alone, each single-job machine of sigma contributes one) shows that k's machine ends by C(tau). Further: for a job k completing at the makespan of a list schedule of a nonincreasing p, the smaller of C(sigma) and 3 p_k is at most C(tau) for every tau, and C(sigma) <= 3 p_k certifies optimality; equality 3m C(sigma) = (4m - 1) C(tau) on m >= 2 machines forces 3 p_k = C(tau), equal loads before k, every load of tau equal to C(tau) and no positive job after k; Della Croce-Scatamacchia's Proposition 4, q (m - 1) C(sigma) <= ((q + 1)(m - 1) - 1) C(tau) when another machine holds q jobs before k and q + 2 <= m, proved from Chen's property; Dósa's theorem (2004, Theorem 2: Graham's example is the only tight one): every positive multiple of Graham's 2m + 1 jobs in any order attains the bound, and for a nonempty positive instance on m >= 2 machines a list schedule in nonincreasing order, or an LPT schedule in any order, attains 3m C(sigma) = (4m - 1) optMakespan only when the instance is a positive multiple of Graham's jobs, so the inequality is strict for every number of jobs other than 2m + 1; and for every fixed n >= 2m + 1 the constant 4/3 - 1/(3m) is the supremum (IsLUB) of C(sigma)/optMakespan over the LPT schedules of the positive instances with n jobs (the proof approaches it with Graham's jobs followed by small jobs; Dósa's Remark 1 asserts a strict gap for every n != 2m + 1, which can therefore hold at most for n < 2m + 1, not formalized here). Forty-one compared statements over nine fully specified definitions; the finite facts behind every statement are replayed exactly in the standard library by scripts/check_lpt.py. As of 2026-10-11 no kernel-checked proof of the 4/3 - 1/(3m) bound, of either equality family or of the optimality statement was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, anthropics/formal-math, the Isabelle AFP, the Rocq package index, GitHub code search in Lean or arXiv; the AFP's Approximation_Algorithms proves a 3/2 bound for sorted greedy and the factor 2 for greedy, and two Lean repositories prove m * C <= sum p + (m - 1) * p_max over lists of naturals. No priority is claimed.
entries.title: Graham's bounds for list scheduling and LPT on identical machines: 2 − 1/m, 4/3 − 1/(3m) and their tight instances

entries.abstract: Theorem D: for real theta, the nine points (cos k theta, sin k theta), k = 0, ..., 8, of the Euclidean plane are distinct, lie on the unit circle and are not Euclidean Ramsey when tan(theta/2) is transcendental; and whenever they are distinct, they are Ramsey if and only if cos theta and sin theta are algebraic (that is, iff e^(i theta) is algebraic), if and only if tan(theta/2) is algebraic. This is an iff for a whole one-parameter family, where earlier explicit examples with a transcendental parameter (OpenAI's Proposition 7.7 and Corollary 7.5) settle single sets: the same nine-point pattern is Ramsey or not exactly as e^(i theta) is algebraic or transcendental. Nine is the exact threshold (eight consecutive multiples are Ramsey for every theta; by hand, in spherical-ramsey), and at theta = e the question becomes whether e^(i e) is algebraic, which appears to be open. Ramsey is OpenAI's definition from result 172 (for every r >= 2 there is D such that every r-colouring of R^D contains a monochromatic congruent copy). The statements are given in OpenAI's vocabulary plus the two-line definition of the nine points, and again with no definitions beyond Mathlib. The non-Ramsey direction mirrors OpenAI's nine-point proof (their Proposition 7.6): the coordinate field is Q(tan(theta/2)), its tensor square embeds in Q(T, U), and the denominator-cleared 9x9 evaluation matrix is nonsingular, certified at (T, U) = (2, 3) by an explicit integer triangular factorization checked by decide +kernel; OpenAI's linear obstruction concludes. The converse uses the theorem that finite spherical sets with algebraic coordinates are Ramsey (prior work of JD-Jones-ASES, Rogerhu12 and atimics; proved again here in Lean on OpenAI's development). The proof builds on OpenAI's complete Lean proof of the classification (openai/math fd4aeeb2), whose 35 files used here are included with header-only changes for the Lean module system. This repository is a module-system port, with no statement or proof line changed apart from a namespace rename, of Lean already public as rope AV3 of spherical-ramsey v1.1.0 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23396387), packaged so that Theorem D can be checked on its own. All theorems depend on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.
entries.title: The radian nine-gon is Euclidean Ramsey iff e^(i theta) is algebraic

entries.abstract: Five compared theorems. Among all substitutions on at most three letters whose incidence matrix has a Pisot eigenvalue θ > 1, the least such θ is the plastic number ρ, the real root of x³ = x + 1, attained only by the Padovan rule a ↦ b, b ↦ c, c ↦ ab and its mirror c ↦ ba, up to renaming the letters; both minimal rules are chiral, in opposite directions. Precisely: (1) for a substitution σ on k ≤ 3 letters (images may be empty) and a real eigenvalue θ > 1 of its integer incidence matrix that is a Pisot number, ρ ≤ θ, and θ = ρ exactly when, after renaming the letters, σ is the Padovan rule or its mirror; no primitivity or unit hypothesis; (2) the same classification for every real eigenvalue, with no Pisot hypothesis; (3) a 3 × 3 natural matrix with characteristic polynomial x³ − x − 1 is the Padovan matrix after one simultaneous permutation of rows and columns; (4) Siegel's bound ρ ≤ θ for Pisot numbers of degree at most three (Siegel 1944, restricted; not new; proved through the minimal Mahler measures of registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004); (5) under the Padovan rule the word ca is a factor of the fifth iterate from the seed a, and ac is a factor of no iterate from any seed; under its mirror, the reverse. The uniqueness was stated without proof by Mercat (2020) for substitutions on three letters; the contribution is a kernel-checked proof of the combined statement, for every real eigenvalue and with no primitivity, unit or non-erasing hypothesis (in the equality case these are consequences: θ = ρ forces k = 3 and characteristic polynomial x³ − x − 1), together with the chirality of both minimal rules. No first-formalization claim is made. That ρ itself is a Pisot eigenvalue of the Padovan matrix, so that the bound is attained, is proved in Supplement.lean and not compared. Companion of registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006.
entries.title: The Arithmetic of Time: the slowest settling clock on at most three letters is the Padovan substitution, unique up to mirror image, and both minimal rules are chiral

entries.abstract: A formal proof of the classical asymptotic omega(binomial(2n,n)) times log n divided by n tending to log 4. The proof combines prime-power estimates, central-binomial bounds, a prime-factor cutoff, and elementary logarithmic limits; it does not use the prime number theorem. This strengthens the earlier finite lower-bound package to a full asymptotic theorem. It does not solve the uniform conjecture in Erdos problem 685 and claims no new mathematical theorem.
entries.title: Distinct prime divisors of central binomial coefficients

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of classical eigenvalue bounds for a finite simple graph G on a nonempty vertex type, with λ_max and λ_min the largest and smallest eigenvalues of its real adjacency matrix: the average degree is at most λ_max and λ_max is at most the maximum degree (Collatz–Sinogowitz); G is (⌊λ_max⌋ + 1)-colourable (Wilf 1967); if G has an edge, every proper colouring uses at least 1 − λ_max/λ_min colours (Hoffman 1970); and if G is k-regular with k ≥ 1, every independent set has at most n(−λ_min)/(k − λ_min) vertices (Hoffman's ratio bound). Mathlib has the spectral theorem for Hermitian matrices but none of these bounds.
entries.title: Spectral bounds on the chromatic and independence numbers

entries.abstract:
This development formalizes in Lean 4 the results of the paper "The local dynamical structure of Δ* sets via a new Furstenberg family algebra", which strengthens the connection between the combinatorics of difference sets and the dynamics of group rotations.
Let S be a discrete semigroup. A set A ⊆ S is syndetic if there is a finite F ⊆ S with S = ∪_{f ∈ F} f⁻¹A; a Δ set if there is a sequence s₁, s₂, … in S with s_j ∈ s_i A for all i < j; and a Bohr_0 set if it contains the preimage of an open neighborhood of the identity under a semigroup homomorphism from S to a finite-dimensional torus. Dually, a set is thick, a Δ* set, or a set of Bohr recurrence according as it meets every syndetic, every Δ, or every Bohr_0 subset of S. Bohr_0 sets in the integers are the almost periodic sets of classical interest, and Δ* sets are combinatorially large, being syndetic and rich in additive patterns.
The definition of a Δ set used here is the one given for general semigroups by Hindman, who calls these rQ sets, Q for quotient; in a commutative semigroup his left- and right-handed variants agree. It does not require the witnessing sequence to be injective, and so is slightly more inclusive than the classical difference-set definition. In the positive integers the two agree exactly: if A consists of positive integers and s_j − s_i ∈ A for all i < j then the sequence is strictly increasing, so A contains the difference set (S − S) ∩ ℕ of the infinite set S = {s₁, s₂, …}, and conversely. The two notions separate only in a semigroup containing an element a with sa = s for some s, where the constant sequence makes every set containing such an a a Δ set. In the integers the element 0 is of this kind, so a Δ set in the present sense is either a classical difference set or a set containing 0, and a Δ* set is exactly a classical Δ* set that contains 0.
The main result (Theorem A) is that Δ* sets in an arbitrary commutative semigroup carry local Bohr structure: if A ⊆ S is a Δ* set, then for every thick H ⊆ S there is a thick H′ ⊆ H and a Bohr_0 set B with A ∩ H′ = B ∩ H′. This generalizes results of Bergelson, Furstenberg and Weiss and of Host and Kra from the positive integers to arbitrary commutative semigroups by a purely topological-dynamical route in place of the ergodic- theoretic arguments used in the integer case. Theorem B is the dual formulation, in terms of Δ sets and sets of Bohr recurrence, that the proof actually establishes: if A ⊆ S admits a thick H such that A ∩ H′ is a set of Bohr recurrence for every thick H′ ⊆ H, then A is a Δ set. Theorem C exhibits a second instance of local structure by the same method: in a countable commutative semigroup, every C* set agrees with an IP* set on a thick subset of any prescribed thick set.  Theorem C also formulates the equivalent dual statement, just as Theorem B is in relation to Theorem A.
Theorem D supplies the algebraic framework the arguments rest on. A Furstenberg family on a set S is an upward-closed collection of subsets of S. On the Furstenberg families of a non-empty set, two binary operations, family meet and family join, are described and shown to be associative, commutative and monotone. Together with the family dual, they satisfy De Morgan-type laws. Family join has appeared before in the literature; family meet, as presented here, is believed to be new. The algebra reduces the equivalence of Theorems A and B to a short computation and makes similar reformulations in Ramsey theory routine.
The proofs of Theorems A and B depend on a companion result, formalized here but the subject of another Palomar entry, that the regionally proximal relation is an equivalence relation for minimal actions of commutative semigroups. The development runs to roughly 20,000 lines of Lean across 17 files and formalizes every lemma, proposition, corollary and theorem of the paper; the registered statements are Theorems A, B, C and D. Proved along the way, and not available in Mathlib, is the classical fact that the characters of a compact abelian group separate its points.
entries.title: The local dynamical structure of Δ* sets via a new Furstenberg family algebra

entries.abstract: The countable-support Sigma-product of arbitrary first-countable topological factors, relative to an explicit basepoint and with the ordinary product-induced topology, is Frechet-Urysohn. An adaptive finite-coordinate schedule constructs a sequence from each set converging to any of its closure points. The index set may be arbitrary, including empty, and no separation assumption is used for this theorem. Companions give countable tightness and subspace inheritance, density in the full product, T1 countable-closure support control and sequential closedness, and nonsequentiality of an uncountable discrete Boolean cube. No normality, W-space, arbitrary Frechet-factor, compactness or novel-mathematics result is asserted.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Fréchet–Urysohn Σ-products of first-countable spaces

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Dirac's 1960 theorem: in a k-connected finite simple graph with k ≥ 2 (more than k vertices, and connected after deleting any set of fewer than k vertices), any set of at most k vertices lies on a common cycle. In particular, in a 2-connected finite graph any two vertices lie on a common cycle. Cycles are Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.Walk.IsCycle`. Mathlib does not have this theorem.
entries.title: Dirac's theorem: k vertices of a k-connected graph lie on a common cycle

entries.abstract: Lean formalization proving the planar Polya-Szego conjecture for the first buckling eigenvalue. For open planar sets of positive finite area, it proves the sharp area inequality and characterizes equality by exact equality with an open disk. It retains the original Sobolev-space, variational eigenvalue and Bessel definitions, and includes the disk eigenvalue and buckling–Dirichlet comparison.
entries.title: Planar Pólya–Szegő Buckling Inequality

entries.abstract: Let U(n,k) be the full prime-power part of the binomial coefficient n choose k supported on primes at most k. For all sufficiently large n, there exists k at most n with k at most 514(log n)^2 and U(n,k) greater than n squared. For arbitrarily large n greater than one, U(n,k) equals one throughout k at most (log n)/8. This independent Mathlib-only implementation adapts the known residue averaging and prime-power obstruction of APSSV26 with coarse Chebyshev constants. It does not formalize that paper's sharper coefficients or Bae's stronger registered lower bound. The optimal order remains open and no mathematical novelty is claimed.
entries.title: Elementary bounds for Erdos problem 684

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of classical structure theorems for finite simple graphs. Chordal graphs: every minimal a–b separator is a clique, a nonempty finite chordal graph has a simplicial vertex, and a connected non-complete one has two non-adjacent simplicial vertices (Dirac 1961); a finite graph is chordal iff it has a perfect elimination order (Fulkerson–Gross 1965), iff it is the intersection graph of subtrees of a finite tree (Gavril 1974); a nonempty finite chordal graph has treewidth ω − 1, and every finite graph has ω ≤ tw + 1. Split graphs: split iff the graph and its complement are chordal, iff no induced 2K₂, C₄ or C₅ (Földes–Hammer 1977). Threshold graphs: threshold iff no induced 2K₂, C₄ or P₄ (Chvátal–Hammer 1977), iff split and a cograph (no induced P₄). Mathlib has none of these graph classes; their definitions are stated in the Challenge.
entries.title: Chordal, split, threshold and cograph structure

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Tutte's f-factor theorem: a finite simple graph G has a spanning subgraph H with deg_H v = f v for every vertex v if and only if, for all disjoint vertex sets S and T, q(S, T) ≤ ∑_{v ∈ S} f v − ∑_{v ∈ T} f v + ∑_{v ∈ T} deg_{G−S} v, where q(S, T) is the number of connected components C of G − (S ∪ T) for which ∑_{v ∈ C} f v + e(C, T) is odd and deg_{G−S} v is the number of neighbours of v outside S. Mathlib has Tutte's 1-factor theorem but not the f-factor theorem.
entries.title: Tutte's f-factor theorem

entries.abstract: For every real additive constant C and natural cutoff K, every sufficiently large natural n admits K < k < n with omega(n-k) at least log(k)/log(log(k)) + C. Here omega counts distinct prime factors. This independently implemented proof uses a fixed primorial residue window, elementary Chebyshev estimates and Stirling bounds. It refutes the known additive strengthening and does not resolve the main multiplicative question. No mathematical novelty is claimed.
entries.title: Additive strengthening of Erdos problem 679: a known refutation

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the graph removal lemma of Erdős, Frankl and Rödl for an arbitrary fixed finite graph H on k vertices: for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0, depending only on H and ε, such that every finite graph on n vertices with fewer than δ nᵏ labelled copies of H can be made H-free by deleting fewer than ε n² edges; equivalently (far form), a graph from which at least ε n² edges must be deleted to destroy all copies of H has at least δ nᵏ labelled copies. Also included is the counting lemma used in the proof: if parts s x (one for each vertex x of H) are robustly dense with density at least d along the edges of H, with 2kη ≤ dᵏ and #(s x) ≥ 4k/dᵏ, then at least (dᵏ/4)ᵏ ∏ #(s x) injective maps send H into G with f x ∈ s x. Mathlib has the regularity lemma and the triangle removal lemma, but not the removal lemma for a general H.
entries.title: The graph removal lemma for every fixed graph

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two classical degree-sequence conditions for Hamiltonicity of a finite simple graph on n ≥ 3 vertices with degrees d₁ ≤ ⋯ ≤ dₙ. Chvátal's theorem (1972): if for every i < n/2, dᵢ ≤ i implies d_{n−i} ≥ n − i, then the graph is Hamiltonian (stated without sorting: if at least i vertices have degree at most i, then at least i + 1 vertices have degree at least n − i). Pósa's theorem (1962): if for every k with 1 ≤ k < (n − 1)/2 fewer than k vertices have degree at most k, and, for odd n, at most (n − 1)/2 vertices have degree at most (n − 1)/2, then the graph is Hamiltonian. Mathlib has Hamiltonian cycles but neither theorem.
entries.title: Chvátal's and Pósa's degree conditions for Hamiltonian cycles

entries.abstract: A product of at most continuum many separable topological spaces is separable. The proof constructs a countable family of finite binary tables that realizes every finite assignment of natural-number labels, then applies dense sequences in the factors. No separation, metrizability, compactness or countable-base assumption on the factors is needed. Empty factors and empty index sets are allowed. A companion theorem proves the sharp criterion for discrete Boolean cubes: Bool^I is separable exactly when the index cardinality is at most continuum. This is the classical countable-density case; no arbitrary-cardinal or algebraic generalization, novelty or priority is claimed.

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Hoffman–Singleton theorem on Moore graphs of diameter two. For a finite k-regular graph of diameter at most two: the Moore bound n ≤ k² + 1; if moreover the girth is at least five, then n = k² + 1 and the graph is strongly regular with parameters (k² + 1, k, 0, 1); and, if k ≥ 2, then k ∈ {2, 3, 7, 57}. Mathlib has strongly regular graphs and the spectral theorem for Hermitian matrices, but not this theorem.
entries.title: Moore graphs of diameter two: the Hoffman–Singleton theorem

entries.abstract: A uniform finite-view reduction at the paper's counting-optimal k-bit vertex budget for odd maximum degree 2k-1. Given one total finite-view orientation rule with a sufficient one-bit advice guarantee, one decoder family is chosen before graph order, topology, markers, advice and payload. Every connected graph on Fin n with n>16(k+1) and degree at most 2k-1 admits an encoder recovering every edge bit at either endpoint from a 2^k-symbol vertex alphabet. The same total decoder is local across different connected graphs and arbitrary labelings, with no marker validity or encoded-input premise. Its explicit physical radius depends only on k and the oracle's radius, not n. Eight selected endpoints also cover storage capacity, advice-first coding, complete-graph counting, and bounded connected cell geometry. The external orientation algorithm, computability, general identifier assignments for the assembled theorem and mixed-component assembly remain outside the selected formal scope.
entries.title: Optimal Local Decompression: Uniform Finite-View Reduction

entries.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization around the quadratic form Q(n) = sum_{i,j in G} K(g(j) - g(i)) n_i n_j of Y. Huang (arXiv:2604.13238) on the gap diagram G of the numerical semigroup <a,b>, in two parts. Part A (Huang's results, two generators): the symmetric bilinear form B of Q satisfies B(1_D, 1_E) = dinv(D, E) for subdiagrams D, E (Huang's Theorem 1.2, formalized by AxiomProver and included in `Dinv/AxiomProver.lean`); from it this work proves Q(1_D) = dinv(D) and Q(1_D) > 0 for nonempty D (Theorem 1.1), B >= 0 on the cone of nonnegative decreasing functions, and the bound Q(n) >= n_i^2 / |G| for every coordinate i (Theorem 1.3, so Q(n) >= ||n||_inf^2 / |G|), which settles Huang's positive-definiteness conjecture for Q on that cone; Theorem 1.3 had not been formalized. Part B (the author's manuscript "A Linear Algorithm for Huang's Quadratic Form on Numerical Semigroups and Density Asymptotics", Flamandzki, 2026): for generators p_1,...,p_n the generalised kernel K^(n)(d) is the inclusion-exclusion sum over sub-multisets S of the generators of (-1)^|S| times the indicator of d >= sigma(S), where sigma(S) is the sum of S; it is a step function whose jumps are the parity function pi(s) = K(s) - K(s-1). Part B states and proves: (1) for two generators a < b, Q equals the sliding-window form sum_k n_k (W+_k - W-_k); (2) for any nonempty generator list, Q(n) is a sum over the breakpoints s of K of pi(s) times the tail pair-sum T(s) = sum_{j-i >= s} n_i n_j, with at most sigma + 1 breakpoints, and the number w of active windows (intervals between consecutive breakpoints on which K is nonzero) is at most sigma, and at most 2^n - 2 for n >= 2 distinct positive generators; and (3) for strictly increasing generators p_k >= 2 with log p_n = o(n), the density w(n)/(2^n - 1) is o(P(n)) where P(n) = prod (1 - 1/p_k), equivalently delta(n)/P(n) tends to 1 for delta(n) = P(n) - w(n)/(2^n - 1). The complexity claims of the manuscript (running times of the algorithms) and its computational tables and conjectures are not formalized. The substance of Part B is the exact breakpoint decomposition of Q, the identification of the inclusion-exclusion kernel with its recursive form, and the asymptotic squeeze. Zero sorries; depends only on the three standard Lean axioms. The file `Dinv/AxiomProver.lean` is third-party code under the MIT license (see NOTICE); everything else is Apache-2.0.
entries.title: NumericalSemigroups: Huang's quadratic form, its positivity, and its n-generator kernel windows

entries.abstract: Every continuous map from an arbitrary product of nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces into a metrizable space factors continuously through a countable subproduct. A uniform-space proof establishes countable coordinate dependence for uniformly continuous maps into separated countably generated uniform spaces. The factor for a fixed coordinate set is unique. Countably many maps share a countable coordinate set. Continuous injections into metrizable targets force only countably many nontrivial factors, giving the exact metrizability criterion for nonempty compact Hausdorff products. Empty index and empty selected-coordinate sets are allowed. These are classical results and no novelty or priority is claimed.

entries.abstract: This is a Lean 4 formalization of Theorem 1.1 from the paper "Bounds for anisotropic Carleson operators" by J. Roos, which generalizes the Lacey-Thiele proof for Carleson's theorem. The classical Carleson theorem on pointwise almost everywhere convergence of Fourier series is derived as a special case.
entries.title: Formalization of Carleson's theorem via the Lacey-Thiele approach

entries.abstract: Kernel-checked proof, for every Coxeter system on three generators a, b, c with m(a,c) = p, m(b,c) = q, m(a,b) = infinity and p, q >= 2, of the growth-series identity in the ring of integer power series: (sum_n a(n) X^n) * (1 - (X + ... + X^(p-1))(X + ... + X^(q-1))) = (1 + X)(1 + ... + X^(p-1))(1 + ... + X^(q-1)), where a(n) is the number of group elements of Coxeter length n; together with its instances (2,3,inf), (2,4,inf), (3,3,inf) and, for (2,3,inf) = PGL(2,Z), the sphere sizes 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 12, 16, ..., the Padovan identity a(n) = Pad(n+5) for n >= 2, the two-sided bounds 2 rho^n <= a(n) <= 4 rho^n (n >= 2), and the growth rate a(n)^(1/n) -> rho, the plastic number, the unique real root > 1 of x^3 = x + 1; and, for the whole family, monotonicity and symmetry in (p, q), the growth rate of every hyperbolic member, and the minimality of the plastic number. Twenty compared theorems: (1) the general identity for all p, q >= 2; (2) non-vacuity, a Coxeter matrix of that type exists for all p, q >= 2; (3)-(5) the three instances; (6) the (2,3,inf) sphere sizes a(0..4) = 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and the recursion a(n+5) = a(n+3) + a(n+2) for all n; (7) that the recursion fails one step earlier, a(4) != a(2) + a(1); (8) a(n) = Pad(n+5) for n >= 2, for any sequence with the Padovan initial values and recursion; (9) existence and uniqueness of the plastic number; (10) the bounds; (11) the n-th-root limit; (12) monotonicity: a(n) of a (p,q,inf) system is at most a(n) of a (p',q',inf) system for p <= p', q <= q'; (13) symmetry in p and q; (14) 2 rho^n <= a(n), n >= 2, for every hyperbolic member; (15) for (p,q) != (2,2) exactly one tau > 1 solves (tau^-1 + ... + tau^-(p-1))(tau^-1 + ... + tau^-(q-1)) = 1; (16) a(n)^(1/n) -> tau; (17) tau strictly increasing in (p,q); (18) rho <= tau with equality exactly at (2,3), (3,2), so the plastic number is the minimal growth rate of the family; (19) tau < 2; (20) tau -> 2 as p, q -> infinity (for every sigma < 2 there is N with tau > sigma whenever p, q >= N). The family statements (12)-(20) give the growth rate of every hyperbolic (p, q, inf) group as the unique root tau > 1 of an explicit equation, strictly increasing in the labels, with the plastic number as the family minimum attained only at (2,3,inf) and (3,2,inf); they restrict to this family, and kernel-check there, Terragni's monotonicity (2016, Thm. A), Floyd's planar minimality (1992, p. 482) and the continuity of the growth rate (Floyd 1992; Yukita 2024). The mathematics is classical and no novelty is claimed for it: the growth series of a Coxeter group is rational and determined by its finite parabolic subgroups (Steinberg 1968; Humphreys 1990 Section 5.12); growth of planar hyperbolic Coxeter groups is Floyd 1992 and Cannon-Wagreich 1992, and the (2,3,inf), (2,4,inf) and (3,3,inf) sphere sequences are OEIS A096231, A179070 (shifted) and A054886, with generating functions derived there from Cannon-Wagreich Prop. 3.1 and, for A096231, the Padovan form a(n) = A000931(n+10) recorded; Floyd 1992 (p. 482) proves (2,3,inf) minimal among cusped planar groups and Kellerhals 2013 gives an alternative proof; Bucher-Talambutsa 2016 Prop. 18 proves statement (11) itself by a normal form and, with Mann's bound, the minimality of rho for PGL(2,Z) over all generating sets. The (p, q, inf) family is hyperbolic exactly when (p, q) differs from (2, 2); the affine (2, 2, inf) is included in (1). The contribution claimed is the kernel-checked general identity for all p, q at once, and the family statements (12)-(20) derived from it, from Mathlib's CoxeterSystem alone — Mathlib at this pin has no growth series, no exchange or deletion property and no parabolic-subgroup API — by constructing the amalgam normal forms, lifting their action to the group, proving Coxeter length equals normal-form length, and counting. No "first formalization" claim is made. Application, cited and not a claim of the entry: the (2,3,inf) group is the Weyl group of AE_3 = PGL(2,Z) (Feingold-Frenkel 1983) and, in the Damour-Henneaux-Nicolai billiard description of the Belinski-Khalatnikov-Lifshitz limit (a conjecture for generic singularities, Henneaux-Persson-Spindel 2008 Section 2.9), the reflection group of the billiard of 3+1-dimensional vacuum gravity near a spacelike singularity (Damour-Henneaux-Nicolai 2003 Section 8; Henneaux-Persson-Spindel 2008 Section 3.1), where a(n) counts the chambers reachable from the fundamental chamber after exactly n wall collisions over all initial data, so (10)-(11) give the growth rate of those outcomes (elementary reflection-group geometry, not formal content). Hypotheses are inline: the Coxeter system enters through Mathlib's CoxeterSystem with the three matrix entries as hypotheses, rho through its defining equation and 1 < rho, the Padovan sequence through its initial values and recursion; the compared statements use only core Mathlib vocabulary (CoxeterMatrix, CoxeterSystem, CoxeterSystem.length, Nat.card, PowerSeries.mk, Finset.range/Ico sums, Filter.Tendsto, Filter.atTop, nhds, real powers) — zero custom definitions. The pinned source of each Coxeter-specific imported definition, and of Nat.card and PowerSeries.mk, is quoted verbatim, with permalinks, in MATHLIB_DEFINITIONS.md (the remaining vocabulary is standard Mathlib and is not quoted), and DefinitionAudit.lean kernel-checks the facts the statements rely on (the entry 0 encodes infinity; length is the minimal word length; spheres are finite and Nat.card is their cardinality; every Coxeter matrix has a Coxeter system).

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization project for the connected size-Ramsey equality rhat_c(4K2, C4) = 17. The intended proof uses a universal C4 vertex-transversal bound 4 tau_4(G) <= |E(G)|, a classification of the connected equality cases through sixteen edges (C4, the 4-wheel, K_{3,3} minus an edge, the octahedron), an avoiding-colouring construction from a three-vertex transversal, and an explicit twelve-vertex, seventeen-edge host. entries.abstract: For an arbitrary compact Hausdorff space, metrizability and second countability are each equivalent to the existence of a countable network of arbitrary subsets. A genuine Urysohn-function construction from pairs of network elements supplies continuous separation, and a compatible metric induces exactly the original topology. Supporting results give bounded-real-coordinate closed embeddings, preservation under continuous surjections, arbitrary-subspace heredity and compact-subspace metrization. Empty spaces and arbitrary universes are allowed. This is classical mathematics; no novelty or priority is claimed.

entries.abstract: Lean formalization of coordinatewise Rényi and Tsallis entropy monotonicity for finite independent Bernoulli sums on the closed half cube, for every real order in [0,2], as stated in Hillion-Johnson Conjecture 4.4. The complete core proves both entropy comparisons and the finite inverse-score association inequality. Concrete coefficient-law and entropy definitions are checked separately. VERIFICATION.md defines exact-source Linux acceptance and distinguishes historical association-only checkpoints.
entries.title: Rényi and Tsallis entropy monotonicity for Bernoulli sums

entries.abstract: Kernel-checked certificates for the multiplicative compositum of the two registered Mahler minimizers — rho, the real root of x^3 = x + 1 (the plastic number: Smyth's nonreciprocal minimum, Siegel's smallest Pisot number) and Q, the real root > 1 of x^4 = x + 1 (the degree-4 entry of the minimal-measure tables) — together with the Bedford-Kim spectral family whose limit rho is, and (new in version 2) the identification of that family with the Coxeter-element spectra of the E_m star trees. Twenty-two compared theorems. The spectral half: (1) for n >= 7 the family chi_n(x) = x^(n+1)(x^3 - x - 1) + (x^3 + x^2 - 1) has a canonical root in [117/100, rho), largest below rho, strictly increasing, tending to rho; (2) every chi_n is strictly positive on [rho, infinity); (3) chi_7 = (x - 1) * L exactly, over any commutative ring, with L Lehmer's degree-10 polynomial; (4) L has a root in [117/100, rho). The compositum half, for the degree-12 minimal polynomial of rho * Q (written out in full in every compared statement): (5) an exclusion witness — a nonreal quartic root z with 1 < |rho * z| < rho * Q; (6) the twelve embedding products ARE the conjugates of rho * Q, both directions; (7) there are exactly twelve of them; (8) rho * Q is an algebraic unit, via an explicit degree-11 cofactor over any commutative ring — the (3, 4, 12) triple in the normal form alpha * beta * gamma = 1; (9) the degree-12 polynomial is not reciprocal (neither its reversal nor the reversal's negation), placing it in the regime of Smyth's theorem; (10) degree multiplicativity — deg minpoly(rho*Q) = deg minpoly(rho) * deg minpoly(Q) = 12; (11) the compositum in sup form Q(rho) join Q(Q) = Q(rho*Q), of degree 12, with the two simple extensions linearly disjoint; (12) the complete unit-circle census — EXACTLY 5 conjugates strictly outside, EXACTLY 7 strictly inside, NONE on the circle, so rho * Q is neither a Pisot nor a Salem number; (13) the house — every conjugate other than rho * Q has modulus strictly below rho * Q; (14) the exact Mahler measure M = rho^2 * Q^2 * psi, where psi is the real root > 1 of psi^4 = psi^3 + 1; (15) the registry bridge — M(X^4 - X - 1) = psi and M(rulerPoly) = (rho * Q)^2 * M(X^4 - X - 1), re-proving in-repo the quantity pinned in registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004; (16) the order-12 Hadamard product recurrence — the termwise product of any solutions of the cubic and quartic shift recurrences satisfies the order-12 recurrence whose characteristic polynomial is exactly the degree-12 polynomial, in any Q-algebra; (17) the annihilator ideal of the product power sequence n |-> (rho * Q)^n is EXACTLY the principal ideal of the degree-12 polynomial — the classical order <= 3 * 4 bound is an equality, forced by the polynomial's kernel-held irreducibility. THE COXETER BRIDGE (version 2), for the star trees E_m = T(2,3,m-3) with generalized Cartan matrix A given entrywise and Coxeter element c = s_0 s_1 ... s_{m-1}, each simple reflection the matrix s_i = 1 - e_i e_i^T A of the geometric representation: (18) for every m >= 4, (X - 1) * charpoly(c) = X^(m-2)(X^3 - X - 1) + (X^3 + X^2 - 1) — the classical E_n Coxeter-polynomial identity (recorded in Gross-Hironaka-McMullen 2009, Section 1, and proved there as Cor. 4.3 for n >= 4), whose right-hand side is chi_{m-3}: the spectral half of this entry IS the E_m Coxeter spectrum; (19) with the E_10 Cartan matrix written out, the Coxeter polynomial of E_10 is Lehmer's polynomial; (20) for every m >= 10 the Coxeter polynomial of E_m has a root lambda_m in [117/100, rho) with no real root above it, the lambda_m strictly increasing and tending to rho; (21) for every m >= 10 the complexified Coxeter element has an eigenvalue lambda in (1, rho) and every complex eigenvalue is unimodular, lambda, or 1/lambda; (22) that lambda dominates the modulus of every eigenvalue and is a Salem number, for every m >= 10, with the Salem predicate written out as in the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000003. Two disclosures of version 1 are discharged by (21)-(22) for n >= 7: the Salem property of the Bedford-Kim roots is now kernel-held, and the interval (1, 117/100) is now swept (the only eigenvalues off the unit circle are lambda_m and its inverse). The results address four research audiences: the degree problem for products and composita of algebraic numbers (the certified (3,4,12) witness at a canonically distinguished pair, in the field's own unit-product normal form); the Mahler-measure tradition (the measure of the composed product of the two degree-minimal polynomials, in closed form in the second-smallest Pisot number); composed products of polynomials (a certified rational instance where the finite-field coprimality criterion is unavailable and irreducibility is proved by elimination); and, new, Coxeter groups and Salem numbers (McMullen; Gross-Hironaka-McMullen; Hironaka's Lehmer program): the E_m Coxeter spectra, their Salem radii and their limit rho as one kernel-checked family — with the Lean audience served by concrete exercise of the Mahler-measure, linear-disjointness, Matrix.charpoly and spectrum APIs. Like the golden ratio, rho * Q is an algebraic unit of norm -1; the compared cofactor identity is that norm computation, certified. No novelty claim is made for the measure identity (the entry is not aware of it in the literature; the claimed contribution is the kernel certificate), none for the mathematics of (18)-(22), which is classical (the claimed contribution is the kernel-checked bridge from the registered Bedford-Kim family to the E_m Coxeter elements, for every m >= 4 (bridge) and every m >= 10 (spectrum, Salem) at once), no "first formalization" claim is made anywhere, and whether rho is ATTAINED as a dynamical degree is open in the literature — no statement claims it. Hypotheses are inline: rho, Q, psi enter only through their defining equations plus root-selection inequalities, the E_m Cartan matrices only through their entries, and the compared statements use only core Mathlib vocabulary (Filter.Tendsto, nhds, the complex norm, minpoly, Polynomial.rootSet, Set.ncard, Polynomial.mahlerMeasure, IntermediateField adjoin/sup, Module.finrank, Finset.range sums, Matrix.charpoly, Matrix.diagonal, List.finRange/List.prod, matrix literals, Matrix.map, spectrum, IsIntegral, Polynomial.aeval) — zero custom definitions. The name prefix "ruler" in statement names is the source project's term for the product rho * Q; nothing in any statement depends on it.
entries.title: The compositum of the two Mahler minimizers: exact measure, conjugate census, house, and minimal product recurrence, with the Bedford-Kim plastic family, Lehmer's polynomial, and the E_m Coxeter bridge

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Erdős' 1959 theorem: for every g and k there is a finite graph with girth greater than g and chromatic number greater than k. The formalization proves the structural form given by Erdős' probabilistic argument: for every g and every ε > 0, for all sufficiently large n there is a graph on n vertices with no cycle of length at most g in which every independent set has fewer than εn vertices; hence, for all large n, a graph on n vertices with girth greater than g that is not k-colourable. Mathlib has girth and chromatic number but not this theorem; Mycielski's construction (registered separately by another author) gives triangle-free graphs only.
entries.title: Erdős' theorem on graphs of large girth and large chromatic number

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of three classical results on edge-disjoint trees and forests in finite simple graphs, none of which is in Mathlib. (1) The Nash-Williams–Tutte tree packing theorem: a graph has k edge-disjoint spanning trees if and only if every partition of its vertices into m parts has at least k(m − 1) edges between different parts. (2) Nash-Williams' arboricity theorem: the edges can be covered by k forests if and only if every nonempty vertex set S spans at most k(|S| − 1) edges. (3) The corollary that every 2k-edge-connected graph has k edge-disjoint spanning trees. Mathlib has no matroid union theorem and no graphic matroid; the proofs are direct edge-exchange arguments.
entries.title: The Nash-Williams–Tutte tree packing theorem and Nash-Williams' arboricity theorem

entries.abstract: For a specified planar homogeneous cubic family, positive definite real homogeneous quartic Lyapunov certificates exist with strict derivative exactly when the absolute parameter is below an explicit algebraic boundary, and with weak derivative exactly through that boundary. Its value is about 2.1281535330886186. At the positive endpoint the entire cone of quartics with nonpositive derivative is one explicit nonnegative ray, without any positivity assumption. The negative Lie derivative of the endpoint quartic is a cubic square with three distinct real zero lines. Exact integer certificates separate degrees two and four at parameter two, and degrees four and six at nine fourths. The formal statements use actual partial derivatives and allow unrestricted real coefficients.
entries.title: Sharp quartic Lyapunov boundaries and sextic separation for a planar cubic family

entries.abstract: Five real symmetric PSD 3×3 integer matrices and five complex Hermitian PSD 2×2 Gaussian-integer matrices each have sum 100I and exact norm-of-averaged-product ratio 10329/10000 at n=k=5. The Lean statements use Mathlib positive semidefiniteness over the real and complex fields and the Euclidean operator norm. The rational formalization of De Sa's dimension-five norm-19/16 example is included as a supporting benchmark. The real symmetric dimension-two case is not resolved.
entries.title: Low-dimensional exact counterexamples to the Recht–Ré inequality

entries.abstract: For every fixed finite graph F of chromatic number r+1 at least three and every positive epsilon, there is an edge threshold M such that every finite simple F-free graph G with m at least M satisfies F2(A_G) <= 2(1-1/r)m - (2(1-1/r)-1)Delta(G) + epsilon m. F2 is the sum of the squares of the two largest positive adjacency eigenvalues with missing terms padded by zero. The graphs may be disconnected. A companion theorem establishes agreement with the two largest ordered eigenvalue squares in the same eventual range. Enough edges force an F-free graph to be noncomplete; BN nonedge interlacing gives a nonnegative second ordered eigenvalue, so its positive-two energy equals the first two ordered eigenvalue squares. The proof checks ordinary clique removal through regularity and clique counting, derives weighted deletion, reuses the proved BN rank-two Gram inequality, and supplies the spectral lift, hub separation and uniform assembly.
entries.title: A sharp asymptotic spectral bound for forbidden subgraphs

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of Ehard, Glock and Joos, "Pseudorandom hypergraph matchings" (Combin. Probab. Comput. 2020): Pippenger's theorem on almost perfect matchings in almost regular hypergraphs with small codegrees (Theorem 1.1); the existence of a matching M in any r-uniform hypergraph with Δ(H) ≤ Δ, codegrees ≤ Δ^{1−δ} and at most exp(Δ^{ε²}) edges such that ω(M) = (1 ± Δ^{−ε}) ω(E(H))/Δ simultaneously for up to exp(Δ^{ε²}) weight functions (Theorem 1.2, with ε = δ/(50r²)); the generalization to weight functions on ℓ-tuples of edges, under the same exponential cap on the number of edges and of weight functions (Theorem 1.3, the main theorem, with ε = δ/(50L²r²)); the concentration inequality for pattern weights under a uniformly random colouring (Theorem 3.1); and the existence of partial Steiner systems whose subgraph counts behave as in the random model (Theorem 4.1). The formal proof is self-contained over Mathlib: Freedman's and Bernstein's inequalities are proved inside the project, and the Molloy–Reed colouring theorem used as a black box in the paper is replaced by a self-contained nibble.
entries.title: Pseudorandom hypergraph matchings (Ehard–Glock–Joos)

entries.abstract: A compact Hausdorff space is metrizable if and only if its diagonal is a Gδ subset of its square with the product topology. The proof supplies a cofinal countable family of finite intersections of closed diagonal neighborhoods and an actual metric inducing exactly the given topology. The underlying type is arbitrary and may be empty. A general supporting theorem proves countable neighborhood character of every closed Gδ set in a compact normal space. This is classical mathematics; no novelty or priority is claimed.
