entries.title: Sneider's Gδ-diagonal metrization theorem

entries.abstract: Disproves an explicitly corrected global threshold formulation of Erdos problem 662. For each radius, the conjecture bounds the average number of nearby points in every sufficiently large one-separated planar set by the unit triangular lattice's neighbor count. An exact rational oblique lattice and separated finite replicas violate the bound at radius six.
entries.title: Erdos 662: corrected global threshold conjecture

entries.abstract: This is a Lean 4 formalization of the main theorem of the papers arXiv:1907.00405 and arXiv:2107.14616 by Ben Krause and Joris Roos. The result concerns l^p boundedness for a  discrete maximal singular oscillatory operator of Stein-Wainger type, also called a discrete Carleson operator.
entries.title: Formalization of a discrete Carleson theorem of Stein-Wainger type

entries.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the paper "A converse to the discrete four-vertex theorem", answering Tabachnikov's Problem 2. For every n >= 4, every cyclic sequence of positive numbers with two distinct plateau maxima and two distinct plateau minima is the sequence of circumradii of consecutive vertex triples of a simple, strictly convex, coherent polygon (circumcenters inside the vertex angles). Together with Dahlberg's discrete four-vertex theorem, also proved here, this characterizes the nonconstant radius sequences of such polygons. The realization can be chosen C^1 in the data near every nonconstant admissible sequence, but an explicit path of hexagon data admits no continuous choice of realizing polygons. The analogous characterization for circles tangent to three consecutive supporting lines (the converse to Wegner's four-edge theorem) is also proved.
entries.title: A converse to the discrete four-vertex theorem

entries.abstract:
This is a Lean 4 formalization of Theorems 1.1 and 1.4 from the paper "Diameter-free reverse inequalities and superorthogonality" by A. Cushman, C. Demeter and S. Wu.
Theorem 1.1 is a reverse square-function estimate in L^4 under a superorthogonality hypothesis that is weaker than the Type IV superorthogonality of Gressman-Pierce-Roos-Yung.
Theorem 1.4 applies a similar estimate to the three-dimensional light cone, yielding a refinement of the reverse cone square-function estimate of Guth-Wang-Zhang.
entries.title: Formalization of a sharp cone square-function estimate via superorthogonality

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the stability theory of Turán's theorem. (1) Füredi's sharp stability theorem for cliques: a K_{p+1}-free graph on n vertices with at least t(n, p) − t edges (t(n, p) the number of edges of the Turán graph) has a p-partite subgraph with at least e(G) − t edges, via Füredi's partition inequality e(G) + Σᵢ e(G[Vᵢ]) ≤ e(K(V₁, …, V_p)); also edit distance at most 3t to a complete p-partite graph. (2) The Erdős–Simonovits stability theorem for every forbidden graph L with χ(L) ≤ p + 1: for every ε > 0 there are δ > 0 and n₀ such that every L-free graph on n ≥ n₀ vertices with at least (1 − 1/p) n²/2 − δn² edges differs from a complete p-partite graph in at most εn² edges, derived as in Füredi's paper from the regularity method. For this, the project extends Mathlib's regularity theory, which only treats triangles, with (3) the clique counting lemma in ε-uniform parts, (4) the clique removal lemma (fewer than δn^r copies of K_r can be destroyed by deleting fewer than εn² edges) and (5) the embedding lemma for any fixed graph with a proper colouring into pairwise uniform dense parts. Mathlib has Turán's theorem, Szemerédi's regularity lemma and triangle counting/removal, but none of (1)–(5).
entries.title: Füredi's stability theorem and the Erdős–Simonovits stability theorem

entries.abstract: On a fixed flat Lorentz frame with metric diag(1,1,1,-1), sources are symmetric 4x4 tensor-valued functions of the six real components of an antisymmetric field. Twelve kernel-checked statements. Among all symmetric homogeneous quadratic sources (210 free coefficients), the six infinitesimal Lorentz covariance equations together with zero trace select the Maxwell stress (the electromagnetic energy-momentum tensor) up to a unique real scale, and a displayed certificate of 209 linear coefficient equations is equivalent to both laws. Among the same homogeneous quadratic sources, conservation alone - vanishing divergence on every source-free Maxwell/Bianchi first jet - selects the same line, with covariance, trace zero and Hodge invariance derived rather than assumed. The globally C^3 symmetric conserved sources are exactly an explicit seventeen-parameter family (constant, a six-parameter cross term, and the stress), and with covariance zero field value is equivalent to zero trace and to the stress line. Under the sourceful exchange law at current stiffness k (the real factor multiplying the jet current), every everywhere-differentiable symmetric source is a constant plus the Maxwell stress of scale exactly k, and conversely, with no polynomial, degree, C^3, covariance or trace hypothesis; zero field value selects the stress. Explicit counterexamples show that covariance and zero trace are each necessary in the quadratic selection, and that covariance and the zero-field normalization are each necessary in the C^3 selection. Uniqueness of the Maxwell stress tensor is classical (Fock 1964; Kerrighan 1982; Navarro-Sancho 2012; the classification of Maxwell conservation laws by Anco-Pohjanpelto 2001); the contribution is the constructive, kernel-checked development on the explicit register at finite regularity, with finite certificates, the covariance-free routes, and the differentiable-only sourceful statement. Pisot Dimensional Theory motivates the frame; no physical coupling is selected.
entries.title: Selection of the electromagnetic source tensor by covariance, conservation and the exchange law

entries.abstract: Formalization of waist inequalities for different settings: (1) Gromov's waist theorem for the round sphere S^n (the original proof in Memarian arXiv:0911.3972 has gaps; here a spherical adaptation of Klartag's proof is used); (2) An explicit positive lower bound on the unnormalized (n-k)-dimensional Hausdorff measure (Mathlib's muH[n-k], defined via sum of (diam U_i)^{n-k} without the unit-ball normalization factor omega_{n-k} / 2^{n-k}, in the chordal metric on S^n) of a fiber on the round sphere S^n: muH[n-k](f^{-1}(y)) >= 1 / (12 * 4^n * 3^k), yielding the positive lower bound (omega_{n-k} / 2^{n-k}) / (12 * 4^n * 3^k) for conventionally normalized Hausdorff measure (motivated by Gromov's 2003 conjecture of the sharp bound vol(S^{n-k}), which remains open for 1 < k < n; proved via Akopyan modification of Klartag's argument, Waists.sphere_hausdorff_waist); (3) The Gaussian waist inequality on (R^n, gamma_n) (Gromov 2003, Klartag arXiv:1608.04121); (4) The waist of the open unit cube (0,1)^n (Klartag arXiv:1608.04121); (5) The waist of the Euclidean ball B^n(R) with arbitrary center and radius (Akopyan-Karasev, arXiv:1608.06279); (6) The waist of a spherical ball of radius R < pi in S^n (Akopyan-Karasev, arXiv:1702.07513); (7) The waist of a hyperbolic ball of radius R in H^n (Akopyan-Karasev, arXiv:1702.07513); (8) The waist of an ellipsoid with semi-axes a_1 <= ... <= a_n (Akopyan-Karasev, arXiv:1608.06279, Corollary 1); (9) The waist of a box / parallelotope (0, a_1) x ... x (0, a_n) (Akopyan-Karasev, arXiv:1608.06279, Corollary 2). Supporting developments include: classical and tree Borsuk-Ulam theorems derived from combinatorial Tucker-type lemmas; Prékopa-Leindler and Brunn-Minkowski inequalities; spherical cap quasiconcavity; Archimedes' projection; and Frostman center measures.
entries.title: Waist

entries.abstract: A reproduction of a complete Lean proof that every set A of natural numbers with positive ordinary upper asymptotic density contains an infinite subset B whose distinct pair sums, after one integer translation, all lie in A. This is the exact ordinary-density statement of Erdős Problem 656, an instance of Kra–Moreira–Richter–Robertson Theorem 1.2(i).
entries.title: Erdős Problem 656: translated restricted pair sums

entries.abstract: A T0 space is metrizable if and only if it admits a sequence of open covers such that every intersecting pair of members at the next level has union contained in one member at the current level, and the point-stars form a neighborhood basis. Without separation the same criterion characterizes pseudometrizability. The proof constructs a countably generated co-membership uniformity with exactly the supplied topology. Covers have unrestricted cardinality; empty spaces are included. Classical mathematics, with no novelty or priority claim.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Alexandroff–Urysohn cover metrization

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 development of Section 3 of Lagarias, Mallows and Wilks, Beyond the Descartes circle theorem (Amer. Math. Monthly 109 (2002) 338-361), in the Lorentz form. An oriented sphere in R^n with centre x and signed radius r has the augmented curvature-centre row (|x|^2/r - r, 1/r, x/r); an oriented hyperplane <h, y> = delta with unit normal h has the row (2 delta, 0, h) (LMW Definition 3.2, (3.7)-(3.9)). Tangency is distance-encoded in LMW's oriented sense: two spheres dist^2 = (r + s)^2 (external tangency for two positive radii, internal when one radius is negative), a sphere and a hyperplane <h, x> - delta = -r, two hyperplanes opposite unit normals, LMW's oriented tangency pair by pair, and the converses deliver tangency in this sense; the compatible orientations of an oriented Descartes configuration (disjoint interiors, with the given orientations or all reversed) are proved separately for every solution, after multiplying each row's power polynomial by the total curvature, and for a valid, pairwise tangent family with positive total curvature for its own open interiors. Kernel-checked, for every n >= 1 (LMW's Section 3 assumes n >= 2; their Section 8, (8.4), is the identity on the line): the augmented matrix W of n + 2 pairwise tangent spheres of nonzero curvature, and of n + 2 pairwise tangent spheres and hyperplanes, satisfies W^T Q_n W = [[0, -4, 0], [-4, 0, 0], [0, 0, 2 I_n]] with Q_n = I - (1/n) 11^T (Theorem 3.3); every real solution W is the augmented matrix of exactly one family of valid, pairwise tangent oriented spheres and hyperplanes, and, when its second column has no zero, of exactly one pairwise tangent family of spheres (the converse of Theorem 3.3); the Soddy-Gosset relation (sum 1/r_i)^2 = n sum (1/r_i)^2 with and without hyperplanes (Theorem 1.2, (1.2)) and its form b^T Q_n b = 0 ((3.2)); the curvature-centre identity M^T Q_n M = diag(0, 2 I_n) (Theorem 3.2, (3.5)); at n = 2 the complex Descartes theorem (sum b_i z_i)^2 = 2 sum (b_i z_i)^2 and sum b_i (b_i z_i) = (1/2)(sum b_i)(sum b_i z_i) (Theorem 2.1, (2.2)-(2.3)); det Q_n = -2/n; and the three statements for Mathlib's EuclideanGeometry.Sphere (pairwise IsExtTangent, or one enclosing sphere to which the others are IsIntTangent, with curvature -1/r_e). The matrix identity is proved as LMW's Section 4 argument (Lemmas 4.3-4.4, (4.9)-(4.10)) run directly in Euclidean coordinates: W^T Q_n W is the target exactly when the rows of W have Lorentz norm 1 and pair to -1 under G = [[0, -1/2, 0], [-1/2, 0, 0], [0, 0, I_n]], since W G W^T = 2I - J and (2I - J)(Q_n/2) = I. Also proved: both halves of the converse of the Soddy-Gosset theorem, LMW's Theorem 3.1, about which they write "We do not know an easy proof of this result; a proof appears in [16]" ([16] is Graham-Lagarias-Mallows-Wilks-Yan III, whose arXiv versions 1-2 prove both halves as their Theorem 2.2 from the same base configuration and the transitivity of the Lorentz group, a section the published version omits). Existence: every nonzero b with (sum b_i)^2 = n sum b_i^2 is the curvature vector of a pairwise tangent family of spheres, where b_i is nonzero, and hyperplanes, where b_i = 0, and of a family of spheres when no b_i vanishes, by one Q_n-reflection from the configuration of two parallel hyperplanes and n unit spheres in the proof of GLMWY III's Theorem 6.1, or from its inversion in the unit sphere. Congruence: two valid, pairwise tangent families with the same curvatures, index by index, are carried one to the other by exactly one Euclidean motion x -> x O + t with O^T O = I, reflections and hyperplanes included, with O = (1/2) X^T Q_n X' and t = -(1/4) a^T Q_n X' for augmented matrices [a | b | X] and [a' | b | X'] and the motion's action on points, spheres and hyperplanes; W_1^-1 W_2 preserves the target form and fixes the curvature coordinate, and every such matrix is a motion matrix (GLMWY III's arXiv v1-v2 argue instead by the rigidity of a simplex of centres); its uniqueness and parameters are proved here. A motion preserves validity, curvature and tangency, so two valid, pairwise tangent families are congruent exactly when their curvature vectors agree. For every solution W: the total curvature B is nonzero, the open sets {y : B F_i(y) < 0}, F_i(y) = b_i |y|^2 - 2 <v_i, y> + a_i the power polynomial of row i (negative exactly inside a ball, outside a ball of negative radius, or on the side of a hyperplane its normal points to), are pairwise disjoint, at most two rows are hyperplanes, and no three boundaries pass through a finite point; for a valid, pairwise tangent family the total curvature is nonzero, at most two members are hyperplanes, and when the total curvature is positive the open interiors are pairwise disjoint. The converse of Theorem 3.2 in every dimension under the hypothesis of a nonzero first column (every real M with M^T Q_n M = diag(0, 2 I_n) and a nonzero first column is the curvature-centre matrix of exactly one family of valid, pairwise tangent oriented spheres and hyperplanes), which GLMWY I, Theorem 3.1 and its Remark, prove at n = 2 with that hypothesis and which LMW's printed converse ("any real solution M") and GLMWY III's arXiv v1-v2 Theorem 2.3 omit, together with the matrix at n = 2 with columns 0, e_0 - e_1, e_2 - e_3 (GLMWY I's configuration (3.15) with its first column zeroed; the matrix of four oriented lines with normals +-e_0, +-e_1), which solves the equation and is the curvature-centre matrix of no valid, pairwise tangent family. The existence of a configuration in every dimension (that configuration); for n >= 2 the Apollonian generators S_k = I + (2/(n-1)) e_k 1^T - (2n/(n-1)) e_k e_k^T of GLMWY III, (4.1), preserve Q_n and carry configurations to configurations, with the row formula (S_k W)_k = (2/(n-1)) sum_{i != k} W_i - W_k, and Soddy's two spheres (LMW, footnote 3; GLMWY III, Section 4.1), in the signed sense: the oriented spheres and hyperplanes tangent to n + 1 members of a configuration are exactly the missing member and its Apollonian reflection, two distinct objects whose curvatures sum to (2/(n-1)) times the sum of the others' curvatures. The planar Soddy-Gosset relation for four circles of positive radius, pairwise externally tangent or with one enclosing circle, is already in Lean in facebookresearch/atlas-lean (descartes_circle_theorem, not registered); rjwalters/lean-genius and carlok/LeanFrontier treat the planar relation as a definition (its two roots, the same over the complex numbers, integer reflections and parity; LeanFrontier checks it for one family of Ford circles and their tangent line), with no derivation from tangency; no other formalization of these statements was found by the dated searches.
entries.title: The augmented Descartes theorem in every dimension, its converses, and Soddy's two spheres

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Cauchy–Binet formula for determinants of products of rectangular matrices over commutative rings (not in Mathlib), of Kirchhoff's matrix-tree theorem (the number of spanning trees of a finite graph is any principal cofactor of Mathlib's Laplacian matrix), and of Cayley's formula (n^(n−2) labelled trees on n ≥ 1 vertices), derived from the matrix-tree theorem for the complete graph.
entries.title: The Cauchy–Binet formula, Kirchhoff's matrix-tree theorem and Cayley's formula

entries.abstract: Theorem B(b): finitely many distinct points on a circle in the Euclidean plane (centre and radius arbitrary reals), all of whose coordinates are algebraic over Q except for the points with indices in a set T of at most three, form a Euclidean Ramsey configuration. Ramsey is OpenAI's definition from result 172 (for every r >= 2 there is D such that every r-colouring of R^D contains a monochromatic congruent copy). The theorem is stated in OpenAI's vocabulary and again in Mathlib vocabulary (Mathlib's Congruent). With the Möbius invariance of the Ramsey property (mobius-ramsey, Theorem C; the combination is by hand), it shows that every set in the class of Theorem A.10 of the appendix of Pálvölgyi's arXiv:2609.23327 is Ramsey; A.10 shows only that his derivation certificates cannot prove such sets non-Ramsey, and leaves their Ramsey status open. Proof: for at most six points, the six-concyclic-points theorem (prior work of JD-Jones-ASES, here with OpenAI's proved sufficiency); otherwise three algebraic points make the circle algebraic, a translation, rational rotation and scaling normalize it, and an explicit certificate (the separability idempotent of the number field of the algebraic points times a graph form through three points containing the exceptional ones) proves OpenAI's field criterion, after which OpenAI's sufficiency theorem concludes. The proof builds on OpenAI's complete Lean proof of the classification (openai/math fd4aeeb2), whose 28 files are included with header-only changes for the Lean module system. All theorems depend on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only. Provenance: this repository is a port, to the Lean module system and Lean v4.35.0-rc2, of a Lean proof already public as rope AV5 of spherical-ramsey v1.1.0 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23396387; a rope there is a self-contained Lean project checked by Comparator), with the same statements and proofs; it packages that one theorem as a standalone, Comparator-checked repository at a current toolchain (docs/PORT-LOG.md).
entries.title: Algebraic points on a circle plus at most three arbitrary points are Euclidean Ramsey

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the two classical characterizations of degree sequences of finite simple graphs: the Erdős–Gallai theorem (a non-increasing sequence is graphic if and only if its sum is even and every initial segment satisfies the Erdős–Gallai inequality) and the Havel–Hakimi theorem (a non-increasing sequence is graphic if and only if its first term is at most the number of remaining terms, the next d₀ terms are positive, and the reduced sequence is graphic).
entries.title: Graphic sequences: the Erdős–Gallai and Havel–Hakimi theorems

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the classical characterization of Eulerian graphs and of Petersen's 2-factor theorem, for finite simple graphs. (1) Euler–Hierholzer: a finite connected graph has an Eulerian circuit if and only if every vertex has even degree, and the circuit can start at any prescribed vertex. (2) Eulerian trails: a finite connected graph has an Eulerian trail if and only if it has 0 or 2 vertices of odd degree; when the odd vertices are exactly a and b, there is an Eulerian trail from a to b. (3) Eulerian orientations: if every degree is even, the edges can be oriented so that every vertex has equal in- and out-degree. (4) Petersen's 2-factor theorem (1891): every finite 2k-regular graph is the edge-disjoint union of k spanning 2-regular subgraphs. The proof of (4) is built on (1)–(3): the graph is decomposed into edge-disjoint closed trails (using the closed-trail lemma behind the Euler theorems), oriented along them, and the resulting k-regular digraph is split into k permutations by Hall's marriage theorem; each permutation yields a 2-factor. Mathlib already contained the necessity directions of (1) and (2); their sufficiency directions were listed there as open TODO items.
entries.title: Euler's theorem on Eulerian circuits and trails, and Petersen's 2-factor theorem

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Gallai–Hasse–Roy–Vitaver theorem: if an orientation of a finite graph has no directed path on more than k vertices, the graph is k-colourable; and conversely every k-colourable graph has such an orientation. Hence the chromatic number is the minimum over orientations of the number of vertices of a longest directed path.
entries.title: The Gallai–Hasse–Roy–Vitaver theorem

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 development of two structures of finite-dimensional quantum information, in the vocabulary of google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (Open Quantum Problems 13 and 23; the fourteen definitions restated character for character under their Apache-2.0 license, see NOTICE). A basis of C^d is a unitary matrix whose columns are the basis vectors; two bases U, V are mutually unbiased when every entry of U^* V has squared norm 1/d; HasMUBs d k says k pairwise unbiased bases exist and IsMaxMUBCount d k that k is the largest such number. Theorems: for d >= 2, HasMUBs d m implies m <= d + 1 (Wootters-Fields 1989; Bandyopadhyay-Boykin-Roychowdhury-Vatan 2002, Theorem 3.5: the identity and the m(d - 1) traceless combinations of the rank-one projectors are pairwise orthogonal in the d^2-dimensional matrix space), and the hypothesis is sharp since in dimension 1 every two bases are unbiased; restriction to subfamilies; the tensor bound HasMUBs m k and HasMUBs n k imply HasMUBs (m n) k (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2004, Lemma 3) and its corollary over the factorization (HasMUBs d k whenever k <= q + 1 for every exact prime-power divisor q of d), hence three mutually unbiased bases in every dimension d >= 2; for a finite field F of odd characteristic and size q, the standard basis and the q bases with entries psi(a x^2 + b x)/sqrt q (psi a nontrivial additive character) are q + 1 mutually unbiased bases (Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 2), through the identity |sum_x psi(c x^2 + e x)|^2 = q for c != 0 proved by Weyl differencing; for q = 2^n the bases with entries i^(x^T S_a x) (-1)^(b . x)/sqrt q, S_a the {0, 1}-lifted Gram matrix of the trace form (x, y) -> Tr(a x y) of the field with 2^n elements (an equivalent form of the Galois-ring bases of Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 3), through the mod-4 identity Q(x + y) = Q(x) + Q(y) + 2 x^T S y and the nondegeneracy of the trace form; so IsMaxMUBCount (p^k) (p^k + 1) for every prime power, HasCompleteMUBs d iff IsMaxMUBCount d (d + 1) for d >= 2, and the values 3, 5, 9 in dimensions 2, 4, 8 also by explicit kernel-checked tables. Weiner's gap (Weiner 2013, Corollary 3.4): any d mutually unbiased bases of C^d extend, by one more basis, to a complete set of d + 1, the given bases keeping their places, for every d (and in the existence form, HasMUBs d d implies HasCompleteMUBs d), by Weiner's proof with its operator-algebra steps written out. The orthogonal projection Phi onto the matrices with a constant diagonal in every one of the d bases has a Kraus form X -> sum_i K_i^* X K_i whose operators K_i have constant diagonals themselves (Weiner's Lemma 3.2, through his Lemma 2.1, sum_k A_k^* X A_k = Tr(X) 1 for an orthonormal basis A_k of the matrix space, recalled there from Werner 2001); at a fixed point X the Kadison-Schwarz defect sum_i K_i^* X^* X K_i - Phi(X)^* Phi(X) is the sum of the squares (X K_i - K_i X)^* (X K_i - K_i X) and has zero trace, so the K_i commute with one another and with their adjoints (in place of the Schwarz inequality and the multiplicative-domain theorem of Choi 1974 that the paper's Lemma 3.1 uses); and the rank-one projectors of a common eigenbasis of the K_i are fixed by Phi, hence have constant diagonals, hence are unbiased to every basis of the family. Corollaries: k >= d bases give a complete set; for d >= 2, d is never the maximal number (in particular mu(6) != 6), and the maximal number is d + 1 or below d. The maximal number mu(d): two bases in every dimension; HasMUBs (p^k) m iff m <= p^k + 1; mu(d) is unique, exists for d >= 2 and lies in [3, d + 1], and does not exist for d = 1; formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim6_bounds, 3 <= mu(6) <= 7, left with sorry there. Reconstruction (Scott 2006, eq. (9)): a complete set of d + 1 bases determines every matrix, X = sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) P_{s,l} - Tr(X) 1 with P_{s,l} the projector onto column l of basis s (after Ivanović 1981 and Wootters-Fields 1989), and so does a SIC family, X = sum_i ((d + 1) Tr(X P_i) - Tr X)/d P_i (its projectors are linearly independent, Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, section II). Second moments (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2005, Theorems 3 and 5; Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, p. 4; Scott 2006, eq. (8)): for all matrices X, Y, sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) Tr(Y P_{s,l}) = Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y for a complete set and (d + 1) sum_i Tr(X P_i) Tr(Y P_i) = d (Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y) for a SIC family; hence the data Tr(X P_{s,l}), and the SIC-POVM outcomes Tr(X P_i)/d with the factor d(d + 1), give ||X||_HS^2 + |Tr X|^2, the Hilbert-Schmidt distance of two matrices with equal traces, and the purity Tr(rho^2) of a Hermitian rho with Tr rho = 1 (Larsen 1990, not read, as stated by Wu-Yu-Mølmer 2009; Scott 2006, eqs. (32), (36), (55)). A SIC family in C^d is d^2 unit vectors with pairwise squared overlap 1/(d + 1); HasSICPOVM d says one exists. Theorems: N unit vectors of C^d with one squared overlap c != 1 on every pair satisfy N <= d^2 (the absolute bound of Delsarte-Goethals-Seidel 1975, the complex form of Gerzon's bound; the rank-one projectors are linearly independent), and with c = 1 the family may be any length; for d >= 2, d^2 such vectors have c = 1/(d + 1) and resolve the identity, sum_i (1/d) |phi_i><phi_i| = 1, so every SIC family is a POVM (Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004), HasSICPOVM d holds iff C^d has d^2 equiangular unit vectors, and a family at the SIC angle has at most d^2 members; Welch's bound (Welch 1974, the bound for k = 1, in the frame-potential form of Benedetto-Fickus 2003): N unit vectors of C^d have sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 >= N^2/d, by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the identity and the frame operator in the matrix space; hence N >= 2 unit vectors with one squared overlap c on every pair have c >= (N - d)/(d (N - 1)), pairwise squared overlaps at most alpha with alpha d < 1 give N (1 - alpha d) <= d (1 - alpha) (the relative bound), and at most d^2 unit vectors have every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1). Welch's equality case (Mixon-Needham-Shonkwiler-Villar, Proposition 1 and its proof): sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 - N^2/d = ||S - (N/d) 1||_HS^2 for the frame operator S = sum_i |phi_i><phi_i|, so equality holds exactly for a tight frame; at equality in the relative bound every pairwise squared overlap is alpha and S = (N/d) 1 (Strohmer-Heath 2003, Theorem 2.3); d^2 unit vectors with every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1) are a SIC family, and HasSICPOVM d holds iff such vectors exist; and pairwise squared overlaps at most 1/(d + 1) + epsilon give ||S/d - 1||_HS^2 <= (d^2 - 1) epsilon for d >= 1, a bound on the resolution of the identity only. SIC-POVMs exist in dimensions 2 (the tetrahedron), 3 (the Hesse configuration), 4 (the sixteen Weyl-Heisenberg translates of Appleby's exact fiducial, Appleby 2005, eq. (149), credited there to Zauner and to Renes et al.; covariance reduces the 240 overlaps to fifteen, proved by exact trigonometric and radical identities in cos(pi/8), sin(pi/8) and sqrt(2 + sqrt 5)) and 8 (Hoggar's 64 lines: the orbit of (-1 + 2i, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)/sqrt 12 under the three-qubit Pauli group, Jedwab-Wiebe 2015, Example 4, checked by the kernel over all ordered pairs). Sixty compared statements, kernel-only. As of 2026-10-10 no formalization of the general bound, of the prime-power constructions, of the factorization corollary, of the complex absolute bound with its equality case, of Weiner's gap for general d, of Welch's bound, of the two reconstruction formulas for every matrix or of a SIC-POVM in dimension 4 was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, physlib, the other Lean repositories searched, the Isabelle AFP, the Rocq package index or arXiv; none of the second moment of a SIC family with its norm, distance and purity forms, of Welch's deficit with its equality case, of the equality case of the relative bound, of the SIC family from d^2 vectors at or below the SIC angle or of the frame-defect bound was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, physlib or the-omega-institute/trureturing. Read 2026-10-14, after that search: marozols/SIC-existence (public 2026-10-09, Lean v4.34.1, self-assessed, unregistered) states SICs in every dimension and, in RSIC.lean, the N = d^2 equality case, in its own vocabulary, so a dimension-4 SIC and that equality case exist elsewhere in Lean; the statements here are over formal-conjectures' definitions and were proved independently. The neighbours: the dimension-2 MUB case is formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim2; the dimension-6 projector bound and the Kronecker lemma are in the XC0R fork of formal-conjectures (adapted here, see NOTICE); the dimension-2 and 3 SIC overlaps are in zblore/csd-lean4; the-omega-institute/trureturing kernel-checks the same 64 Hoggar vectors and the Hesse SIC in its own vocabulary, proves that the trace pairings with a complete family of rank-one contexts determine every matrix, proves the density-matrix formula under an assumed completeness hypothesis, and proves the second moment of a complete set in operator form with the purity identity for density matrices (complete_context_collision_conservation, 2026-08-28); openai/math holds mu(6) <= 5 and Weiner's gap at d = 6 (six_extend_to_seven), with lemmas for general n (commutator_trace_identity, commute_of_kraus_fixed, exists_joint_projection_basis) that make the same elementary move as the route here, the Schwarz defect of a Kraus map as a sum of squared commutators; the Kadison-Schwarz inequality for Kraus and completely positive maps is in physlib, QuAIR/Lean-QIT and kencyke/quantum-system. Not claimed: anything about dimension 6 beyond 3 <= mu(6) <= 7 and mu(6) != 6 (openai/math holds mu(6) <= 5), SICs in dimensions 5 to 7, that a family near the SIC angle is close to a SIC family, any first formalization.
entries.title: Finite quantum designs: mutually unbiased bases, SIC-POVMs, and the Welch and Gerzon bounds

entries.abstract:
Let J=H_3(O), the real algebra of 3×3 Hermitian matrices over the division octonions, with product a∘b=(ab+ba)/2 and diagonal trace T. A frame p=(p_0,p_1,p_2) consists of trace-one elements satisfying p_i∘p_i=p_i, p_i∘p_j=0 for i≠j, and p_0+p_1+p_2=1. For frames p,q,r, record the 27 pair traces T(p_i∘q_j), T(q_j∘r_k), T(r_k∘p_i), and 27 triple traces T((p_i∘q_j)∘r_k), for i,j,k∈{0,1,2}. How much do these traces determine?

Each trace list in some open neighborhood of the data with pair entries 1/3 and triple entries 1/9, in a fixed twenty-dimensional chart, determines exactly two equivalence classes. Equivalence means one product-and-trace-preserving real linear bijection acting on all nine labeled elements, without relabeling. The sign of the degree-nine scalar Phi distinguishes the classes. With x=p_2−p_0, y=q_2−q_0, z=r_2−r_0, define

B(a,b) = T(a∘b),
U_a(b) = 2a∘(a∘b)−(a∘a)∘b,
Phi(x,y,z) = B((U_x U_y−U_y U_x)z,U_z(x∘y)).

Phi's derivative uses Glennie's degree-eight vector polynomial.

For arbitrary x,y,z∈J, Phi≠0 implies that 1,x,y,z generate J.

Recognition starts from a homogeneous cubic N on finite-dimensional real normed E, with N(e)=1 and g_e=−(1/3)D²(log N)_e positive definite on all E. A supplied linear equivalence ker(DN_e)≃ker T (the trace-zero subspace), matching g_e to B/3 and full vector-valued curvature tensors, yields an Albert algebra equivalence.

Consider 27 fixed parenthesized products of a distinguished element and three chosen elements in a real inner-product space with bilinear multiplication. Exact matching with the Albert table of pairwise inner products, inner products of products with these expressions and full ambient squared product norms determines a unique isometric, product-preserving linear embedding of J onto the subspace they generate under products and linear combinations, preserving the distinguished element and chosen elements.

entries.abstract: For F=K5 minus one edge, a color-critical graph of chromatic number four, the graph formed from K(s,s,s) and K4 by one bridge is connected and F-free for every integer s at least three. It has 3s squared plus 7 edges, and the sum of squares of its two largest ordered adjacency eigenvalues exceeds 4m/3 by at least (656s squared-1366s+62)/(3(37s-1) squared)>0. The family has arbitrarily large edge counts, refuting the exact assertion in KKP Conjecture 1.16 and Li–Liu–Zhang Conjecture 5.4.
entries.title: Connected counterexamples to the exact color-critical two-eigenvalue bound

entries.abstract: A formalization of a partial solution to Erdos Problem 99. It shows that Erdos Problem 99 holds for all sufficiently large n where h(n) is finite. Here, h(n) denotes the number of incongruence, diameter-minimizing sets of minimum separation at least 1.
entries.title: Erdos 99 Partial Solution

entries.abstract: Classifies depth labelings in the modal logics wGL_n for positive n. Every simultaneous formula-valued substitution indexed by atom and depth label preserves theoremhood exactly when the labels satisfy c(k+n)=c(k) at every positive depth k. The interpolation equivalences identify the corresponding labeled property with its ordinary interpolation property and the same periodicity condition; the ordinary interpolation theorems remain explicit inputs. Further results classify period spectra, boxed-atom implications and composition of depth substitutions, and transfer a supplied ordinary interpolant while preserving syntax-tree node count and modal depth.
entries.title: Depth-labeled interpolation and substitution in Sacchetti's modal logics

entries.abstract:
A Lean 4 formalisation of the solvability theory of linear second-order elliptic operators in divergence form on a bounded domain,

  -div(A grad u) + b · grad u + c u = f in Ω,   u = 0 on ∂Ω,

with A uniformly elliptic and every coefficient bounded and measurable. The drift b is unrestricted and the bilinear form is in general non-symmetric. The six compared statements are the results of Evans §6.2: the Gårding inequality, existence and uniqueness of the weak solution with no drift and a nonnegative zeroth-order coefficient, the Fredholm alternative, solvability against the transpose problem, the discrete set of exceptional shifts and boundedness of the inverse. They ask only that Ω be bounded and open, and the compact embedding of H_0^1(Ω) in L²(Ω) is proved. Interior regularity at every order, the maximum principles and the Dirichlet eigenvalue sequence are also proved in the library and appear without a Comparator configuration. Built on Mathlib with only Lean's standard axioms.
entries.title: Solvability of divergence-form elliptic equations (Evans §6.2)

entries.abstract: Explicit finite counterexamples to Theorem A (Theorem 3.1) and Lemma 3.2 of Li and Liang, arXiv:2609.10148v2. In Z/13Z, sets of sizes seven and four satisfy all size hypotheses and have restricted sumset size nine, but neither is an arithmetic progression. A separate example in Z/11Z contradicts the lower bound of Lemma 3.2 as stated.
entries.title: Counterexamples to the restricted-sumset inverse theorem in arXiv:2609.10148v2

entries.abstract: An attributed adaptation of the Flypitch formal proof of two-sided syntactic independence of the continuum hypothesis from its explicitly encoded first-order ZFC theory. Cohen and collapse Boolean-valued models, together with soundness, establish that neither the encoded CH sentence nor its negation is derivable. The development uses an expanded language with definable set operations, collection and Zorn's lemma. It does not supply a formal translation to membership-only ZFC or determine the truth of CH for the ambient Lean reals. This is a reproduction of established work, not a new mathematical solution.
entries.title: Continuum hypothesis independence: a Flypitch reproduction
